  • Half-bound loops (since 15 November 2026): a row with only an input or only an output runs with the default map's other half (the zone's actuator that declares the quantity, else the one named after it, and no run at all without either; or every sensor of the quantity's default tag, one fresh one used), with WARNING: zone ZONE01: loop co2 is half-bound: its output is the default map's (actuator co2) until a CONTROL onboarding chooses it. The cycle's run parameters mark it ("completed": "output").
  • The default map, zone by zone (owner decisions Q11 and Q20, choice D-a): a zone with active loop rows runs on them, and a quantity it has no row for is not controlled; a zone with a CONTROL board and no rows gets one loop per loopable quantity of the unit's recipe type, driving the actuator that declares the quantity in its channel map, else the one of the same name. For each, a reading with exactly one sensor that reports in time uses it; with several, the loop gets no data and an alarm ambiguous_source naming them, until an engineer chooses the reference; with none, no data. The substrate loop reads ground_temperature, and CO2 above its limit runs the fans UP (the earlier map read a tag no board publishes, and switched the fans the wrong way).
  • Freshness: a reading counts while it is at most the loop's maximum age old (90 seconds unless set, at most 3600), by the time the runner received it. A run gives its sensors that long to report before it raises an alarm.
  • Fallback, then hold (owner decision Q8): when the reference has nothing fresh, the fallback sensor controls, with the alarm fallback_in_use; when no source is fresh, the loop sends nothing new, the board keeps the last command, and the alarm is no_fresh_data ("holding the last command …", or "nothing sent yet"). A lack of data never switches the fans off.
  • Alarms are run log lines, for example ALARM ambiguous_source unit=UNIT01 zone=ZONE01 loop=air_temperature sensors=scd30_1,sht45_1: choose the reference in onboarding: one when a loop enters the state, the same line again every 300 seconds while it lasts, and ALARM_CLEARED <kind> unit=… zone=… loop=… when it ends. Alarm e-mails come with a later phase (Phase 9).
  • A recipe step without a setpoint for a loop's quantity (an optional quantity left empty) leaves that loop inactive for the step, with WARNING zone … loop …: the recipe line has no … setpoint: inactive. A loop of a quantity whose phase is light_on sends nothing while the light is off.
  • Commands go to <root>/<UNIT>/<ZONE>/control/<actuator> and name the loop, its state and the sensors used. The grow light command goes to every zone of the run once per pass. At the end of a run, and on a stop, every zone of the run gets the stop command.

Not yet (until Phase 4, owner decisions Q3 and Q8): an algorithm that answers OFF while the reading is within the limits, and the end of a run (all_controllers_off), still switch the fans off. Only a lack of data holds them. An existing Q-learning state of the CO2 channel was learnt with the fans the wrong way round; have qa retire it after the deploy (Control Models tab, Retire…; see Configuration UI).

The health check: Control loops

controlloops (Control loops, after Scheduler UI in health-checks.conf; 65 checks since 13 November 2026) reads the database in one read-only session and only warns, never fails: zones that run on the default map ("… zone(s) run on the default map (no control_loop rows; Q20): UNIT01/ZONE01"), those of them with several sensors on one tag ("no_data + ALARM ambiguous_source: choose the reference in onboarding"), sensor problems on a default-map zone, active loops that break the loop rules ("… re-save in onboarding"), and (since 15 November 2026) half-bound loops ("… loop(s) half-bound, running on the default map's other half until its onboarding chooses it: UNIT01/ZONE01 co2 (no output)"). OK reads "N zone(s) with actuators, all on valid control_loop rows (M active loop(s))". SKIP before migration 010. The default map is meant for the transition (owner decision Q11), so the warning stays until each zone has its loops.

The health check: Controller libraries

controllers (Controller libraries, right after Control loops in health-checks.conf; 66 checks since 17 November 2026) looks inside each running scheduler pod, read-only, and prints only two version numbers: gekko, which the MPC controller needs, and scikit-fuzzy, which the FLC controller needs. Without them both controllers quietly behave as the plain on/off controller (If-Then-Else). The scheduler pod installs both from apps/scheduler/requirements-controllers.txt, where every file is pinned by version and checksum, at each start. The check only warns, never fails: "gekko is not installed: MPC runs as bang-bang", "skfuzzy cannot import packaging: FLC runs as bang-bang", or a version that is not the pinned one. Each of these is fixed by ./apps/scheduler/deploy.sh, run while no run is active. OK reads "pod scheduler-…: gekko 1.3.3, scikit-fuzzy 0.5.0 (the pinned versions)". SKIP without the scheduler. The runner's log also shows each fallback: one line "WARNING mpc fallback: …" or "WARNING flc fallback: …" the first time a controller falls back, then at most one an hour.

Since 17 November 2026 MPC's command is the right way round. Until then, below the band it answered DOWN (cool) and above it UP (heat). No run ever used it, because without gekko it ran as on/off control. The owner approved the fix before the libraries were installed.

Rollout of Phases 1 and 2 (for the owner)

The table and the engineer's two functions widen the access policy's skeleton, so the release ships as two skeleton versions, each approved by qa (owner decision Q19, choice D-e): version 2a adds medcea.control_loop for the runner only (svc_scheduler reads it; no person gains anything, so qa may approve it); version 2c lets engineer execute medcea.zone_loop_context and medcea.save_zone_loops (it widens engineer alone, so the person who approves it may hold no enabled engineer account). Only one version may be open at a time. Phases 1 and 2 deploy together (owner decision Q12).

  1. Before: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --status shows no open version and no waiting decision; no run is running or scheduled and no onboarding is in progress (schd/ and edge/ are read by the running services from the checkout, so a checkout changes the next run and the wizard).
  2. Propose 2a from its commit, d8a91f8: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by <you> --reason "…" --from-git d8a91f8, first with --check-only (it must show only svc_scheduler's read and bar no approver). A qa person approves it in the Access Policy. From here on the branch is never rebased: the proposal and the tests name these commits.
  3. Check out cedc494, the last commit with the 2a skeleton (it holds migration 010, the consumers, the runner, the health check and edge Phase 1; an earlier commit such as d8a91f8 lacks them, and later commits carry 2c, which the skeleton gate refuses until it is applied), and run ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <you> (first --check-only). The table does not exist yet; its grant is applied with the database deploy.
  4. ./apps/database/deploy.sh (migration 010: the table, its run guard and record triggers, the sensor column of the measurement views, the two functions without any grant).
  5. Then, in this order: ./apps/monitor/deploy.sh (before it the Monitor answers 500 "column sensor does not exist"), ./apps/report/deploy.sh (Grafana's panels per sensor), ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh (the example notebooks), ./apps/scheduler/deploy.sh (no run in progress; the runner itself is read from schd/ when each run starts), and ./apps/edge-wizard/deploy.sh (refused while a flash runs). Run ./health-check.sh: Database grants OK, Control loops WARN.
  6. Propose 2c from its commit, af5c1ad, the same way (--check-only first: exactly engineer's two EXECUTE rights, and engineer barred from approving). A qa person approves it.
  7. Check out the branch's last commit and run ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <you>; then ./apps/edge-wizard/deploy.sh again, so the wizard offers the picker and the tile, and ./health-check.sh.
  8. Re-onboard the SENSE board (it gets the sensor names, and the SCD30's temperature and humidity) as an engineer, choosing the zone's loops; then run exercises E34 to E36.

Rolling back: a zone's loops can be stopped in the picker (Stop all loops), which puts it back on the default map. Migration 010's down file (apps/database/medcea_db_migrations_down_010.sql, run by hand) is refused while version 2c's grants exist, and keeps the table's rows aside rather than dropping them.

Known gap, older than this work: under IAM_DB_ROLES=true a maintenance person cannot re-onboard a board at all, because onboarding changes the board's component records and maintenance's database role may only read them. It shows as a refused registration. Until it is fixed, an engineer re-onboards. See Known gaps.

Recipe types and the quantity catalogue

Since 15 November 2026 (migration 011; owner decisions of that day in the decision record) a recipe's controlled values are metadata. What can be controlled, and which recipe type sets what, is one file in git, apps/database/recipe_types.yaml:

  • quantities: each with its code (the loop code, the key in a step's setpoints and the runner's learned-state channel: never rename one, a rename orphans learned state and every recipe's setpoints), label, unit, sense_uoms (the UoM strings a SENSE reading may carry to feed it), default_tag, commands (what its actuator must take), an optional command_map (CO2's), phase (always, or light_on: the limit holds only while the light is on), loopable (false: a limit and a gauge, no loop yet) and the plausible range min, max;
  • recipe_types: PLANT (Plants) and FUNGI (Fungi), each with its quantities, true for required on every step, false for optional, and legacy_unit_type (the old unit label it replaces: Greens, Mushrooms);
  • default_type: the type given to a recipe migration 011 cannot type from its units.

To change it:

  1. Edit the file and run python3 apps/database/recipe_types.py check (it says what is wrong; quote command words, "OFF", since YAML reads a bare OFF as false). Commit.
  2. ./apps/database/deploy.sh re-seeds the catalogue from the file (it checks the file first and applies nothing when it is wrong). A quantity or type still in use (a unit, a recipe, a loop) cannot be removed: the deploy stops on the foreign key.
  3. ./apps/frontend/deploy.sh and ./apps/monitor/deploy.sh give the Configuration UI and the Run Monitor the same file as recipe-types.json; ./apps/edge-wizard/deploy.sh is not needed (the wizard reads the zone's quantities from the database).

People never read the three catalogue tables (medcea.control_quantity, medcea.recipe_type, medcea.recipe_type_quantity): they are the runner's (svc_scheduler, skeleton version 6 of the access policy), and a table every recipe reader could read would widen qa's own reach, so that qa could not approve the version. That is also why a step's limits are one column, recipe_line.setpoints, not a table of their own.

Rollout of the recipe types (for the owner)

  1. Skeleton version 6 from commit 32f0264 (the catalogue for svc_scheduler; nobody is barred from approving it): ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by <you> --reason "…" --from-git 32f0264, a qa person approves it, then check out that commit and ./apps/iam/apply.sh 6 --by <you>. From here on the branch is never rebased.
  2. Relax enforcement for the build (owner decision of 15 November 2026): ./medcea.sh → IAM switches: IAM_ENFORCE false (./deploy-infra.sh), then IAM_DB_ROLES false (./infra/deploy-workbench.sh, ./apps/database/deploy.sh). Draft-only, approved-only and the recipe type rules then only warn; the health check WARNs on both switches. Record the start in the decision record's deviation.
  3. No run running or scheduled. ./apps/database/deploy.sh (migration 011). It refuses, naming them, units whose type is neither Greens nor Mushrooms: set them in the Configuration UI first. It types each recipe from its permitted units, else gives the default type and lists it in a warning; it writes every step's setpoints from its eight limit columns and proves the copy reads back exactly, in the same transaction.
  4. ./apps/scheduler/deploy.sh, ./apps/monitor/deploy.sh, ./apps/frontend/deploy.sh, ./apps/edge-wizard/deploy.sh; the runner reads schd/ from the checkout at each run's start. ./health-check.sh.
  5. Once no run started before migration 011 remains: the deploy of the commit that adds migration 012, ./apps/database/deploy.sh. It checks again that every step's limit values read back from its setpoints (one that does not refuses the whole migration and drops nothing), rebuilds the views run_history and run_watch without the columns, and drops the eight limit columns and the control loop table's two recipe columns. No approval digest moves. While IAM_DB_ROLES is false the onboarding wizard's loop picker is not offered (only under true do a person's calls reach the loop functions), so binding loops waits for the last step.
  6. At the end: ./medcea.sh → IAM switches → Bring IAM to full enforcement. Every recipe's approval digest changed with migration 011 (the steps' content moved into setpoints), so the enforce bundle turns every approved recipe back into a draft; a qa person who did not write it approves each again in the Approvals tab. A recipe missing a required quantity on a step cannot be approved ("approve_recipe: recipe … misses required setpoints: line … lacks …"). Then ./health-check.sh and exercises E37 and E38.

Rolling back migration 012: no run in R or S, then apps/database/medcea_db_migrations_down_012.sql by hand as postgres (it adds the eight columns back, nullable as 011 left them, and writes them from the setpoints; it refuses while a setpoint of those four quantities is not a whole number), then git revert of 012 and ./apps/database/deploy.sh. Rolling back migration 011 as well, after that: no run in R or S, then apps/database/medcea_db_migrations_down_011.sql by hand as postgres (it writes the limit columns back from the setpoints, gives the units their old labels, parks the catalogue in schema medcea_retired_011, and refuses while a step holds a value the old integer columns cannot hold, a light intensity limit, or a half-bound loop), then git revert and the same deploys; the policy's version 6 is rolled back last.

The research sandbox

Research sandbox Phase 2a (owner decisions P, F and S of 18 November 2026, in the decision record) gives the sandbox described in Research sandbox a place of its own on the cluster and a copy of the platform's data to work on, without a live connection to the operational database. It was opt-in: RESEARCH_ENABLED in config.env was false by default. From Phase 2b config.env.example has it true, because the AI Workbench lives in the research zone once the policy places it there; an existing config.env keeps its value. Every research deploy also waits for the applied access policy to have the research zone, which only an approved skeleton version adds. Research Phase 2b (owner decisions of 19 November 2026) moves the AI Workbench into the zone and adds the snapshot reader lake-api; its first commit is built, not deployed (Moving the AI workbench, Rollout of Phase 2b).

Status, 19 November 2026. Deployed: commit A, then access policy version 7 (the skeleton version with the research zone, approved by qa_user, applied with ./apps/iam/apply.sh 7 --by admin), then the RESEARCH_ENABLED enable recipe. Reservation #1 and snapshot 1 are made; the health check passes all 68 checks (exercise E42).

WhatWhereMade by
The research zone: namespace RESEARCH_NAMESPACE (default <namespace>-research, label medcea/zone=research); PriorityClass medcea-research-low (value −100, never the default, never preempts: research pods are evicted first when memory runs short); ResourceQuota research-quota (in all: 4 CPUs and 8Gi requested, 24Gi of memory limits, 20 pods, 12 volumes, 120Gi of storage; from Phase 2b 22 volumes and 220Gi, for about 20 workbench homes; a pod that would exceed it is refused with "exceeded quota"); from Phase 2b the namespace's pod security level baseline (labels pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce and warn); LimitRange research-limits (a default memory limit, no default CPU limit); the zone's NetworkPolicies, labelled medcea/rs-netpol=true: rs-default-deny (nothing in or out for any pod), rs-dns (DNS to kube-dns only) and one rs-<pod> per pod of the zone with its compiled callers and destinationscluster./infra/deploy-research-namespace.sh, which ./deploy-infra.sh runs right after the application network policies
The research database: Helm release research-postgresql (bitnamicharts/postgresql 18.4.0, the platform database's chart; its own NetworkPolicies switched off), volume data-research-postgresql-0 (RESEARCH_DB_STORAGE, 10Gi), database medcea_research with schemas lake (the snapshots), vault (the reservations), and sim, agent_trace, registry (empty until later phases); roles rs_owner (owns everything, cannot log in), rs_export_writer (may only stage rows and close a snapshot) and rs_backup (reads, for the nightly backup)research namespace./apps/research/deploy.sh
Secrets research-export-writer and research-backup (the two logins above, for the export and the backup)platform namespace./apps/research/deploy.sh
CronJob research-export, daily at 03:00 UTC (after the 02:30 backup), and ConfigMap research-export-scriptplatform namespace./apps/research-export/deploy.sh
Migration 013: eleven read functions medcea.research_*() in the platform database, owned by medcea_owner; nobody may execute them until the skeleton version grants them to the export's login svc_research_export (Secret db-svc-research-export, written by ./apps/database/deploy.sh)platform database./apps/database/deploy.sh

What reaches the sandbox, by decision: no person column, not even a pseudonym (P); no names, descriptions, notes, reasons, locations or device identifiers, and parameters reduced to their number and true/false values. The export reads only through the eleven functions, never the tables or views (F). The lake is append-only and each snapshot is a high-water mark (S): nothing, the owner role included, can change or delete a lake row or a reservation.

One export run: it reads the latest snapshot's cut from the research database, takes as the new cut the operational database's clock minus 2 minutes, reads the measurements whose ingest time is after the previous cut and up to the new one, and the small sets (units, zones, recipes and their lines, runs and cycles, control loops, approved parameter sets, the quantity catalogue) whole, in one read-only transaction as svc_research_export. Then, in one transaction on the research side as rs_export_writer, it stages the rows and closes the snapshot: lake.close_snapshot drops every reserved reading, moves the rest into the lake, and records the snapshot with a row count and a SHA-256 digest per set. Any error rolls the whole of it back. The job's log ends with one line: research-export: snapshot N cut <cut> measurements M.

Holding data out: reservations

A reservation keeps one unit's readings (or one zone's) whose measurement time is in [from, to) out of every snapshot from then on, so a model can later be judged on data it never saw. Only a qa person reserves, and a reservation is permanent: it cannot be changed or removed. It must be made before the first export that would carry those readings: a range already in the lake is refused ("already exported: it is no longer held out").

  1. ./apps/research/reserve.sh add --by <your qa username> --unit <UNIT> [--zone <ZONE>] --from <TIME> --to <TIME> --reason "<why>", or ./medcea.sh → Applications → Reserve a held-out range (qa). Times are ISO 8601, for example 2026-12-01 or 2026-12-01T06:00, UTC unless they carry an offset. Without --zone every zone of the unit is held out. The reason must be at least 10 characters.
  2. --by must be an enabled account of the realm that holds the role qa; its username and account id are recorded with the reservation. The script asks you to type yes (medcea.sh's own confirmation stands in for it).
  3. It answers "Reservation #N made: unit … [from, to) is held out of every snapshot from now on". ./apps/research/reserve.sh list (or Applications → List the held-out reservations) shows them all.

Refused, with nothing written: a range already exported, a range ending more than a year from now, an account that does not exist, is disabled or does not hold qa. The exit code is 0 when done, 1 when refused (also a held lock or no confirmation), 2 for a usage error or when the research database or Keycloak cannot be reached. add takes the deploy lock; list does not. Both log to logs/app-research-reserve-<timestamp>.log.

Running an export now

microk8s kubectl -n <namespace> create job --from=cronjob/research-export research-export-now-$(date +%s) runs one at once, as the nightly one would; microk8s kubectl -n <namespace> logs job/<its name> shows its lines. Two exports cannot overlap in effect: a run whose previous cut is no longer the latest snapshot's is refused and writes nothing ("another export ran; start again from lake.latest_cut()"), and one whose cut is not after the latest one is refused too. The health check Research export then reports the new snapshot.

Moving the AI workbench (Phase 2b)

Where the AI Workbench runs follows the applied access policy (The AI Workbench in the research zone). When an applied version places it on the other side, ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh changes nothing and prints "the AI workbench moves with ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh --move" (or "moves back with" it); ./deploy-infra.sh shows that as "Still to do", ./install.sh repeats it before the credentials box, and the health check AI Workbench gate WARNs "deferred: ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh --move". The move is one command, run under the deploy lock:

./infra/deploy-workbench.sh --move

or ./medcea.sh → Infrastructure → Move the AI workbench between the platform and the research zone. At the switchover itself the Policy menu's "Research Phase 2b: apply the skeleton version and move the workbench" runs it between the apply and apply.sh --resume (Rollout of Phase 2b). It works in both directions: the target is the namespace the policy names, the source the other one.

  1. Checks. Refused, with nothing changed, while WORKBENCH_ENABLED is not true; for a move into the zone while RESEARCH_ENABLED is not true or the zone's compiled network policies for the hub, its proxy and the notebooks are not in place ("run ./deploy-infra.sh"); without the target namespace; and while any notebook server runs in the source (ask people to stop theirs, or stop them from the hub's admin page).
  2. Confirmation. It says that the homes are copied on the host with sudo, that the hub's database starts fresh (hub users and their personal API tokens are dropped) and that the old directories are kept, and asks you to type yes (medcea.sh's own confirmation stands in for it). Without a terminal it refuses.
  3. Freeze. It scales the hub and its proxy to 0, so nobody can start a server, and checks again that no pod mounts a home.
  4. Keep the volumes. Every home's volume and the hub database's volume in the source is set to Retain before anything is uninstalled, and listed in the log (claim, volume, directory on the host, size).
  5. Keycloak. Moving into the zone, it disables the client workbench-notebook when the policy no longer names it (never deletes it); it says disabled, already-disabled or absent.
  6. Uninstall and copy. It uninstalls the workbench from the source, then copies each home, claim-<name>, with sudo cp -a (sudo asks "to copy the home claim-<name> into <namespace>") into a new directory under MicroK8s's storage folder, and makes a volume and a claim of the same name in the target bound to it. The administrator's own home, claim-admin, is not copied: the administrator gets no workspace in the zone. The old claim is labelled medcea/moved-to=<target> and kept. A home the target already holds is left alone: skipped when an earlier run copied it there, replaced when it is the stale copy of an earlier move the other way (that old volume is marked medcea/superseded so it is never used again), and otherwise reported as not moved with a warning ("… holds its own claim-<name>, not a copy from …: neither is changed"), for you to compare the two homes and keep one by hand. A volume kept by an earlier move is used again instead of a copy only when the old claim says it was moved there, it is the only such volume and its directory is still on the host; several such volumes are reported and none is used.
  7. Install. Moving into the zone it issues the certificate workbench-tls and the hub's Role first, then installs the workbench in the target and waits for its address to answer.
  8. What is left. It lists what it kept and how to remove each one after checking: the old claims of homes it moved and their volumes (microk8s kubectl delete pvc …, then delete pv …, then sudo rm -rf <directory>), the old hub database's directory, and any copy an earlier failed run left that no volume uses. It gives no removal command for claim-admin (kept, as decided) or for a home it did not move ("was NOT moved … it is the only copy of that home"). No script ever deletes them.

Running it again is safe: a home already copied is skipped, and a run that stopped after the uninstall copies only what is missing, from the old claims, which are still there. Until it has, a plain ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh (or ./deploy-infra.sh) does not install a new, empty workbench in the target: it stops with the "moves with ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh --move" line and names the homes not moved yet, since a person signing in would otherwise get an empty home in front of their real one. A run that stops before the uninstall starts the hub again in the source; the volumes stay Retain and the Keycloak client stays disabled, as it says. A move back (a later skeleton version that places the workbench in the platform again; the skeleton version of 2b itself is never rolled back) copies the homes back, the work done in the zone included, and replaces the stale copies left from the first move.

Until you remove them, the old homes in the platform namespace and the kept directories are still copied by the nightly backup, next to the live homes in the zone: twice the space, and copies of what scientists read into notebooks. Remove them once the people have checked their files in the zone.

Offboarding from the AI workbench

Deactivating a person's platform account ends their workbench sign-in within minutes, but not the personal hub API tokens they made in the hub: remove the person from the hub too (the hub's admin page, Delete User; their home is kept). The health check Workbench accounts WARNs for every hub user without an enabled platform account until that is done.

The snapshot reader

./apps/research/deploy.sh creates the reader's database schema and roles (lake_api, rs_lake_reader, rs_lake_api) and, as its last step, runs ./apps/lake-api/deploy.sh (also ./medcea.sh → Applications → Install the lake reader). That deploy skips with one line and exit 0 while RESEARCH_ENABLED is not true, while the applied policy has no lake-api pod ("skipped: the applied access policy has no lake-api pod yet"), while no policy version is applied, before the research namespace or the research database exists; it refuses to start the reader unless the zone's compiled network policy for it is in place. It writes Secret lake-api-auth (the password RS_LAKE_API_DB_PASS, generated by ./infra/configure.sh), the Deployment and the Service lake-api, and checks from the host that it answers. ./apps/lake-api/uninstall.sh removes those three and never the data; ./apps/research/uninstall.sh runs it first, and its --purge-data also drops the two roles. To rotate RS_LAKE_API_DB_PASS, change it in config.env and run ./apps/research/deploy.sh.

The research database in the nightly backup

The nightly backup (Backup and restore) also dumps medcea_research, as rs_backup, into db/medcea_research.dump, whenever Secret research-backup exists and the research server has the database. The backup always knows the research server's address, whatever RESEARCH_ENABLED says, so research switched on later is backed up without redeploying the backup. Its log and MANIFEST say which case applies: no Secret (# databases skipped (no Secret research-backup, no research database on this install): medcea_research), a server without the database (# databases skipped (absent)), or a server that did not answer (# databases not reached: medcea_research; the platform's own databases are still backed up, and that run is not a failure). A dump that fails once the database is known to exist fails the run, as any dump does. ./apps/backup/backups.sh restore-help FOLDER prints the restore steps in its part B3: suspend the export, drop and restore medcea_research in research-postgresql-0, then ./apps/research/deploy.sh and ./apps/research-export/deploy.sh. Snapshots taken after that backup are lost; the next export continues from the restored database's latest cut.

Workbench homes in the research zone (Phase 2b). Once the AI Workbench runs in the research namespace, the backup copies its homes and the hub's database volume from there as volumes/research-claim-<name>.tar.gz and volumes/research-hub-db-dir.tar.gz, listed in MANIFEST and SHA256SUMS like the others; before the move there is nothing to copy there. restore-help's part C finds the namespace the hub runs in and prints the commands for it. Since a person may have two directories (the copy a move kept next to the live one), each archive has a line in MANIFEST, # volume volumes/<archive> from <directory> newest file <time>, and part C picks the archive of the volume the person's claim uses now (a sed on that line), or else the one with the newest file: never by the archive's name. The old homes the move left in the platform namespace are still copied as volumes/claim-<name>.tar.gz until they are removed.

Passwords

./infra/configure.sh generates the sandbox's passwords (four in Phase 2a, five from Phase 2b) whether or not research is switched on, so switching it on asks nothing: RESEARCH_DB_PASS, RS_EXPORT_WRITER_DB_PASS, RS_BACKUP_DB_PASS and SVC_RESEARCH_EXPORT_DB_PASS. None reaches a command line or a log. To rotate one, put a new value of the characters A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ ~ - into config.env, then:

PasswordLoginRun
RS_EXPORT_WRITER_DB_PASS, RS_BACKUP_DB_PASSrs_export_writer, rs_backup in the research database./apps/research/deploy.sh: it sets both passwords on every run and rewrites Secrets research-export-writer and research-backup; the next export and backup use them.
RS_LAKE_API_DB_PASS (Phase 2b)rs_lake_api in the research database./apps/research/deploy.sh: it sets the password and, through ./apps/lake-api/deploy.sh, rewrites Secret lake-api-auth in the research namespace.
SVC_RESEARCH_EXPORT_DB_PASSsvc_research_export in the platform database./apps/database/deploy.sh, as for every service login (Secret db-svc-research-export).
RESEARCH_DB_PASSthe research server's superuser postgresPostgreSQL takes it only when its volume is first initialised. On an existing volume a new value only rewrites Secret research-postgresql-auth at the next ./apps/research/deploy.sh, and the server keeps the old password. Leave it unchanged; to change it, change the server's own password first, in a psql session in research-postgresql-0, and only then config.env and the deploy.

Switching off and uninstalling

./medcea.sh → Infrastructure → Turn the research sandbox on or off, rollback: sets RESEARCH_ENABLED false, then runs ./apps/research-export/uninstall.sh (CronJob, Jobs and ConfigMap; the snapshots stay), from Phase 2b ./apps/lake-api/uninstall.sh, and ./apps/research/uninstall.sh (Secrets research-export-writer and research-backup first, so the export and the backup stop connecting, then the Helm release). The data is kept: the volume data-research-postgresql-0 with every snapshot and reservation, Secret research-postgresql-auth and the research namespace with its policies stay, and a later deploy finds the same data. An AI Workbench the policy places in the research zone is left running and unmanaged by the switch-off (the recipe's checklist says so), and its notebooks lose the lake; ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh then only prints "skipped: the AI workbench lives in the research zone (the access policy) and RESEARCH_ENABLED is not true". While the namespace is there with the switch off, ./deploy-infra.sh warns (naming the workbench when its hub is there) and prints how to remove it (microk8s kubectl delete namespace <research namespace>, then microk8s kubectl delete priorityclass medcea-research-low), and Research network policies WARNs.

  • ./apps/research/uninstall.sh --purge-data also deletes the volume and Secret research-postgresql-auth: every snapshot and reservation is gone. ./deploy-apps.sh --uninstall --purge-data never passes the flag here: purging the research data is this script's own flag (in ./medcea.sh, Applications → Uninstall the research database, which asks for the project name).
  • ./deploy-infra.sh --reset removes the research namespace (only one labelled medcea/zone=research), its releases and volumes, and the PriorityClass; --uninstall removes the whole cluster. Both, and ./install.sh's uninstall levels, list data-research-postgresql-0 with its directory on the host before they ask.
  • A research deploy that skips (switch off, no research zone, no applied version) leaves a running research database alone and says so; the export's deploy that skips removes the CronJob, keeping the snapshots.
  • Removing migration 013 is a separate, later step: apps/database/medcea_db_migrations_down_013.sql by hand as postgres, refused while svc_research_export may still execute a function, so only after the export is uninstalled and the policy version that grants them is rolled back and applied with ./apps/database/deploy.sh.

Troubleshooting

  • Research network policies FAILs "not the zone's, no medcea/rs-netpol=true label: …". A NetworkPolicy that the policy does not compile is in the research namespace (a Helm chart's own, one made by hand). Policies add up, so it opens the zone past its default deny. Delete it: microk8s kubectl delete networkpolicy -n <research namespace> <name>. ./apps/research/deploy.sh refuses to go on for the same reason ("… is not labelled medcea/rs-netpol=true: it admits more than the research zone allows").
  • Research network policies FAILs "missing: …" or "spec differs: …". Run ./infra/deploy-research-namespace.sh --policy-only (it prints rsnetpol: re-rendered), or ./deploy-infra.sh. If ./deploy-infra.sh printed "The research namespace failed to deploy (above). The platform deploy goes on", fix the cause shown above that line and run ./infra/deploy-research-namespace.sh.
  • Research export WARNs or FAILs on the snapshot's age. Look at the last runs: microk8s kubectl -n <namespace> get jobs -l app=research-export and their logs. Each failed line starts research-export: ERROR: and says that nothing was written; a missing Secret is named ("OP_PASSWORD is empty (Secret db-svc-research-export)": ./apps/database/deploy.sh; "RS_PASSWORD is empty (Secret research-export-writer)": ./apps/research/deploy.sh). Then run one now (above).
  • Research export WARNs "no reservation yet". Nothing is held out for validation. A qa person reserves the ranges before the readings are exported; a range already exported can no longer be held out.
  • Research export FAILs "… measurement rows of snapshot … fall in a reservation". Held-out readings reached the lake, which the snapshot step and the reservation step both prevent, so the lake was written around them. Stop the export at once (microk8s kubectl -n <namespace> patch cronjob research-export -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'), record it in the decision record, and keep the database as it is for the investigation: lake rows cannot be deleted, so only a restore from a backup made before that snapshot (part B3 of restore-help) removes them.
  • The export's deploy says "skipped: …". It names why: RESEARCH_ENABLED not true; the applied policy has no research zone yet; no policy version applied; ./apps/research/deploy.sh has not run; or "the research export needs IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=true (its connection is svc_research_export)". It never connects as postgres instead.

Troubleshooting the workbench in the research zone (Phase 2b)

  • ./deploy-infra.sh says "Still to do: the AI workbench moves with ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh --move". An applied version placed the workbench in the research zone and it still runs in the platform namespace. Nothing is wrong; run the move (Moving the AI workbench), then ./apps/iam/apply.sh --resume --by <you> if the apply recorded it as deferred. Until then AI Workbench gate WARNs and Access policy version FAILs on the open deferral.
  • Sign out shows an error page during the move. The platform's one-hop sign-out passes through the workbench's /hub/logout, which does not answer while the hub is down. The platform sign-in is already ended by then; only the last hop failed. It answers again once the move has installed the hub.
  • A pod in the research namespace is refused with "violates PodSecurity baseline:latest". The namespace's pod security level refuses privileged pods, host networking and host directories. A workbench deploy that brings back the chart's own metadata-blocking init container would be refused like this; the zone's values switch it off (singleuser.cloudMetadata.blockWithIptables: false). Never lower the level to make a pod start: record it and ask the owner.
  • A notebook server does not start: "exceeded quota". Four servers at a time fit the quota. Ask someone to stop theirs, or stop an idle one from the hub's admin page.
  • A notebook says "the lake reader is not reachable (./apps/lake-api/deploy.sh)". Run ./apps/research/deploy.sh (it runs the reader's deploy last) and read the line it prints; Research lake reader names the cause.
  • Research grants and Secrets FAILs. A pod of the research zone names a Secret outside its list, a Role there grants Secrets, a RoleBinding there binds a cluster role, a Service there is a NodePort or LoadBalancer, or the research database's grants drifted (the line of assert_grants.sql is quoted). Remove what the message names; never widen the list by hand.
  • Workbench accounts WARNs. A hub user has no enabled platform account: remove the person from the hub (Offboarding).

Rollout of Phase 2b (for the owner)

Phase 2b ships as commit A (all code; the access policy unchanged, so every compiled artefact stays the same), commit B (a skeleton version: the workbench's pods and lake-api in the research zone with their network paths, the notebooks' live path removed, invariant I19, and the narrowed cells as the factory defaults) and a change version (the cells). Version B is never rolled back, as Superset's version 15: undoing 2b is a new skeleton version proposed from a revert, then the move back. Commit A can be reverted only before B is applied. In order:

  1. Commit A: ./deploy-infra.sh (the research namespace's pod security label and quota), ./deploy-apps.sh --all (it redeploys iam-api, whose compiler changed; the research deploy adds the reader's schema and roles; lake-api skips), ./health-check.sh: 71 checks, Research lake reader SKIP.
  2. Export the engineer's Superset dashboards (Superset), and keep the files outside the repository's apps/superset/dashboards/.
  3. Propose commit B: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by admin --reason "…" --from-git <B> (first --check-only). A qa person approves it with the attestation. Then ./apps/backup/backups.sh now.
  4. Ask everyone to stop their workspace; check out B.
  5. ./medcea.sh → Policy → Research Phase 2b: apply the skeleton version and move the workbench. Under one lock it runs ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <you> (the workbench step is deferred), ./infra/deploy-workbench.sh --move, ./apps/lake-api/deploy.sh, ./apps/iam/apply.sh --resume --by <you> and ./health-check.sh.
  6. ./apps/iam/deploy.sh (the Access Policy's explanations and diffs read the skeleton its pod ships: until then they show the old one and Access policy version WARNs on the skeleton digest), ./deploy-infra.sh once more, then tests/iam-research.sh (a throwaway notebook-labelled pod must time out on every platform service and reach lake-api and the internet on 443), tests/iam-workbench.sh and tests/iam-hosts.sh.
  7. Draft the change version "from defaults" in the Access Policy; qa approves; ./apps/iam/apply.sh N+1 --by <you>. The Run Monitor stops admitting the scientists and Superset is stopped.
  8. Exercises E43 and E44; then the manual's edition and the decision record.

What the proposal of commit B shows (proposed on 20 November 2026 and applied as version 8 the same day). --propose-skeleton --check-only reports a widening of the system only: the new pods' network paths (the hub on 8081, the proxy on 8000 and 8001, the notebooks on 8888, lake-api on 3000 and its path to the research database, and the zone pods' outgoing paths: Keycloak for the hub, the cluster's API on port 16443, the internet on TCP 443 for the notebooks), and as changed sections the four pods' labels, zone and outgoing paths, the internet exception list, the AI Workbench's risk text and the removed notebooks client. No role gains anything, so no role is barred from approving it (qa and auditor included). Invariant I19 is added but not listed: adding an invariant only tightens. With the cells of version 7 the compiled artefacts that move are the platform's network policies (the database API no longer admits notebooks), the research zone's policies (four pods more) and the database functions' list of token clients (workbench-notebook leaves it), and the notebooks' egress list for the workbench chart is no longer compiled at all; nothing a person reaches moves until the change version. The proposal made from commit A and the diff apply.sh N recomputes from commit B are the same, so the order above holds (checked offline: PhaseRS2bBDelta compares commit A's compiler with B's).

Fresh installs from commit B have no Superset. The factory file carries the change version's cells, so no role is given a Superset setting: ./apps/superset/deploy.sh skips ("Superset's policy group gives no role a setting yet") and ./install.sh asks nothing more: no Superset is the decided state (O12 in the decision record), not a step left to do. Superset comes back only with a change version that gives a role a Superset setting (Superset).

Rollout of Phase 2a (for the owner)

The research zone, the export's login and its read rights widen the access policy's skeleton, so Phase 2a ships as commit A (no skeleton change; deploys nothing research) and commit B (the skeleton version: svc_research_export, the group research_export with the eleven functions, the research zone on research_workbench, the zone's pods and clients in network:, invariant I18). There is no change version: no person gains a right. In order:

  1. Commit A: ./deploy-infra.sh, then ./apps/database/deploy.sh (migration 013, the functions with no grant). ./health-check.sh: 68 checks, the two research ones SKIP.
  2. Propose commit B: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by <you> --reason "…" --from-git <B>, first with --check-only. A qa person approves it in the Access Policy. From here on the branch is never rebased.
  3. Check out B and apply it: ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <you> (first --check-only).
  4. Switch it on: ./medcea.sh → Infrastructure → Turn the research sandbox on or off. The recipe sets RESEARCH_ENABLED true and runs, under one lock: ./deploy-infra.sh (the namespace and its policies), ./apps/database/deploy.sh (svc_research_export's password and Secret db-svc-research-export), ./apps/research/deploy.sh (the research database and Secret research-backup), ./apps/backup/deploy.sh, ./apps/research-export/deploy.sh. By hand: the same five, in that order, after setting the switch.
  5. Before 03:00 UTC: a qa person makes the reservations (above).
  6. Run one export now, then ./health-check.sh (Research network policies and Research export OK) and ./apps/backup/backups.sh now followed by verify: its MANIFEST lists medcea_research. Then exercise E42, which proves a reserved range is absent from the snapshot.

Backup and restore

Since 1 November 2026 the component backup (apps/backup/, decision of that day) copies the platform's data every night at 02:30 UTC, 45 minutes before the scheduler's own nightly job. One Kubernetes CronJob, medcea-backup, writes one dated folder per run into BACKUP_DIR on the platform host (config.env; /var/backups/medcea by default):

In the folderWhat it is
db/medcea_db.dumpThe platform database (POSTGRES_DB): every run, recipe, measurement, device, approval, account decision and the access policy history. pg_dump custom format, read with pg_restore.
db/keycloak.dumpKeycloak's database: the realm, every account with its password hash, roles, clients and their secrets.
db/superset.dumpSuperset's own database (since 6 November 2026, only on an install where it exists): the dashboards, charts, datasets and saved queries people built, and Superset's copy of the accounts that signed in. On an install without Superset the job logs "skipped superset (no such database on this install)" and MANIFEST says # databases skipped (absent): superset; that is not a failure. If the job cannot ask PostgreSQL whether the database exists, the run fails rather than leave it out unnoticed.
db/medcea_research.dumpThe research sandbox's database (since research sandbox Phase 2a, only while Secret research-backup and the database exist): the snapshots in the lake and the held-out reservations, dumped as rs_backup from research-postgresql. See The research database in the nightly backup.
db/globals.sqlThe database roles and their memberships, without passwords (a reference: a new install's deploys create the roles with its own passwords).
volumes/claim-<name>.tar.gzEach person's AI workbench home, with their notebooks and their GitHub token if they saved one.
volumes/node-red.tar.gzNode-RED's /data: the flows as they run, flows_cred.json and its key, the palette modules.
volumes/grafana.tar.gzGrafana's database: Editors' own dashboards, folders, annotations, alert rules, the Grafana accounts and sessions.
MANIFEST, SHA256SUMSEvery file with its size and SHA-256, written at backup time; sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS checks them. Since IAM 4.5 MANIFEST also names the access policy history's head, read before the dumps: # policy chain head (read before the dump): <event id> <hash> verify_chain=t (or … unavailable (<why>), which never fails the backup). The dump holds at least that event. The health check's iamanchor compares the newest complete backup's head with the live history.
OKWritten last. A folder without it is a run that failed or is still running; nothing treats it as a backup.

Not copied: PostgreSQL's own volume (the dumps are its consistent copy), the broker's persistence (retained messages, which the boards publish again) and the hub's database (the AI workbench rebuilds it as people sign in). config.env, the platform CA .ca/ and edge/provisioned/ are files in the repository folder, not in the cluster: keep your own copy of them, which a full restore after a reinstall needs.

The backups hold secrets: Keycloak's password hashes and client secrets, pgAdmin's stored files inside the platform database, people's homes with their git tokens. ./apps/backup/deploy.sh creates BACKUP_DIR with mode 700 for the account that runs it (with sudo when the parent folder is not writable), and the job hands every folder to that account, mode 700. Copy them only to storage that is as well protected.

Settings and the job

  • BACKUP_DIR: an absolute path. On the same disk as the data (the deploy warns when it is), a disk failure takes both; point it at another disk, or copy the folders off the host. Changing it takes effect at the next ./apps/backup/deploy.sh; the old folder stays where it is.
  • BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS (14): after a good run, folders older than this are deleted, complete or not. The newest complete folder is never deleted, so a host that was off for weeks keeps its last good backup. Only folder names of the form 20261102-023000Z are ever deleted.
  • The job runs in a pod from the same image as PostgreSQL, so pg_dump has the server's version. The postgres password reaches it only from the Kubernetes Secret rdbms-postgresql, never on a command line or in its log. It reads the volumes' directory (/var/snap/microk8s/common/default-storage) read-only, as a whole rather than volume by volume, because a person's workbench home appears at their first start and the job must find it without a redeploy. It runs as root inside the pod to read every person's files, with no other privilege, no access to the Kubernetes API and a read-only image.
  • A host that was off at 02:30 runs the night's backup when it is back within 6 hours. A failed run is not retried; the health check shows it and the next night runs again.
  • Grafana's and Node-RED's files are copied while they run. A save during the copy (unlikely at 02:30) can leave that copy inconsistent; the next night's is not.

Using it

Command (also in ./medcea.sh → Backups)What it does
./apps/backup/backups.sh nowRuns the job once now, waits for it (up to an hour; --timeout SECS) and prints its log, which names files and sizes only. Takes the deploy lock.
./apps/backup/backups.sh listThe folders, newest first: complete or incomplete, size, number of files, when it finished; and how old the newest complete one is.
./apps/backup/backups.sh verify [FOLDER]Checks every file of a complete folder (default the newest) against its SHA256SUMS, and that no unlisted file was added; then prints the policy chain head the folder recorded (policy chain head: not recorded (a backup from before IAM 4.5) for an older one).
./apps/backup/backups.sh restore-help [FOLDER]Prints the restore steps below with that folder's paths and this install's names. It runs none of them.

The health check's Backups line is OK while the newest complete backup is at most 26 hours old, WARN beyond, FAIL beyond 72 hours, and SKIP before the component is deployed and on its first day. Run ./health-check.sh as the account that deployed the backup: it owns the folder.

./apps/backup/uninstall.sh (and every uninstall level of install.sh) removes the CronJob and leaves BACKUP_DIR with every backup in it. Delete it by hand when it is no longer wanted.

Restoring

The restore is shown, not run: it stops services and drops databases, and only you can decide what to put back. Restore only the parts you need. Check the folder first with ./apps/backup/backups.sh verify FOLDER. In the commands below, F is the folder (for example /var/backups/medcea/20261102-023000Z); restore-help prints them with the real path. psql and pg_restore run in the PostgreSQL pod and read the password there; the dump goes in on standard input.

After a reinstall, restore once ./install.sh has finished, with the old config.env if you kept it, and within BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS: the new install's first nightly run deletes the older folders (except the newest complete one). To be safe, copy the folder you will restore from out of BACKUP_DIR first.

The platform database.

  1. Stop the services that write to it: microk8s kubectl -n medcea scale deployment node-red scheduler monitor config-api dbmgmt access iam-api --replicas=0 (one that is not installed is reported "not found").
  2. Drop it and restore it: 
    microk8s kubectl -n medcea exec -i rdbms-postgresql-0 -- sh -c 'PGPASSWORD="$(cat "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE")" exec psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS medcea_db WITH (FORCE)"'
microk8s kubectl -n medcea exec -i rdbms-postgresql-0 -- sh -c 'PGPASSWORD="$(cat "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE")" exec pg_restore -U postgres -d postgres --create --exit-on-error' < F/db/medcea_db.dump
  3. (2a, since IAM 4.2a) Move the host's policy file aside, so the next deploy writes it again from the restored database: bash -c 'source infra/lib-lock.sh && medcea_lock && source infra/lib-policy-source.sh && policy_state_retire restore'. It moves state/policy-applied.yaml, the queue of account facts and any break-glass copies into state/retired-<time>-restore/ and deletes nothing; ./apps/backup/backups.sh restore-help prints the same step. It keeps the mark state/.policy-versioned, so until the next deploy the onboarding wizard (at a restart) and flash-device.sh refuse to compile rather than fall back to defaults.yaml. Without it every deploy refuses while the file names a version the restored database does not have applied (see Policy source). A dump older than version 1 leaves no version: the next ./apps/iam/deploy.sh bootstraps it again.
  4. ./apps/database/deploy.sh: the migrations, grants and role passwords of this config.env.
  5. Start the services again (the same scale command with --replicas=1), then ./health-check.sh: Access policy history must be OK, which shows the restored hash chain is intact.
  6. (Since IAM 4.5) Compare the restored chain with the head the backup recorded before its dump (restore-help prints it, and the query): SELECT (SELECT ok FROM iam_policy.verify_chain()), (SELECT hash FROM iam_policy.history WHERE event_id = <id>), read-only in the PostgreSQL pod. verify_chain() must be true and event <id> must carry that hash: a chain that ends below it, or holds another hash there, was cut or rewritten after the backup.

After restoring the platform database from a backup older than the newest one, the health check's History chain anchor (iamanchor) FAILs: the newest backup recorded a head the restored history does not have. That is expected; it clears at the next nightly backup (or ./apps/backup/backups.sh now), which records the restored chain's head. Restoring from the newest backup leaves it OK.

Keycloak. microk8s kubectl -n medcea scale deployment keycloak --replicas=0; the same two commands with keycloak and F/db/keycloak.dump; scale it back to 1; then ./deploy-infra.sh, which sets the client secrets, the break-glass account and the realm settings back to this config.env. Every account change made after the backup is lost: deactivations included, so check the User Manager's decisions afterwards.

Superset. Only when the folder has db/superset.dump. microk8s kubectl -n medcea scale deployment superset --replicas=0; the same two commands as for the platform database with superset and F/db/superset.dump; then ./apps/superset/deploy.sh, which sets the owner's password and the MedCEA connection back to this config.env and starts Superset. Restore the access policy's state with it (step 2a): if the restored policy gives no role a Superset setting, the deploy stops Superset instead. restore-help prints it as part B2. A dump made under another SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY holds a connection password Superset cannot read; the deploy writes the connection again.

One person's AI workbench home. The person's workspace is stopped (they sign out, or the AI Workbench admin page → Stop). After a reinstall they sign in once first, so their new home exists, and stop it again. Find the home's directory and put the copy back over it (once the workbench runs in the research zone, use the research namespace instead of medcea and the archive volumes/research-claim-<name>.tar.gz; restore-help prints the right ones):

PV=$(microk8s kubectl -n medcea get pvc claim-<name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}')
D=$(microk8s kubectl get pv "$PV" -o jsonpath='{.spec.hostPath.path}')
sudo tar -C "$D" -xzpf F/volumes/claim-<name>.tar.gz --numeric-owner

That overwrites files of the same name and leaves newer files in place. For one file only, list the archive with tar -tzf and add the file's name as listed (for example ./notebooks/a.ipynb) to the same tar -x command.

Node-RED. microk8s kubectl -n medcea scale deployment node-red --replicas=0; find D as above with the claim node-red; replace its content with test -n "$D" && sudo find "$D" -mindepth 1 -delete && sudo tar -C "$D" -xzpf F/volumes/node-red.tar.gz --numeric-owner; scale it back to 1; then ./deploy-infra.sh and ./apps/node-red/deploy.sh, which put back this install's settings, credentials and the repository's flows. The health check's Node-RED flows vs git then names any flow only the backup had.

Grafana. microk8s kubectl -n medcea scale deployment grafana --replicas=0; find D with the claim grafana; replace its content as for Node-RED from F/volumes/grafana.tar.gz, then close the directory again with sudo chmod 0700 "$D" (the archive brings back the volume's open mode; Grafana also closes it at each start); scale it back to 1; then ./deploy-infra.sh (Grafana's break-glass password) and ./apps/report/deploy.sh (the platform's dashboards).

A backup or a restore writes nothing into the platform's records. The job's log is in the Job's pod while Kubernetes keeps it (the last three of each outcome): microk8s kubectl -n medcea get jobs -l app=medcea-backup. ./apps/backup/backups.sh logs in logs/. A restore of the platform database brings back the records of its night; anything recorded after it is gone, and nothing records that it happened, so write the restore down in your own operations log.

The manual in the portal

The portal serves this manual at https://portal.<domain>/manual/, linked as Platform manual from the user menu of every signed-in app (/_account/api/me gives it as manual, built from PORTAL_URL; a menu on another host links the portal's address; see the platform manual in the portal). Everyone the portal admits may read it; there is no access policy change behind it, because the portal's gate covers every path of its address. The decision is in the decision record ("The manual in the platform", 3 November 2026).

What is served is always built from docs/manual/chapters/ at the moment of publishing, never the committed docs/manual/index.html, which may be older: docs/manual/build.py --out <temporary file> --standalone, so publishing never changes the working tree. The page is stored gzipped (about 160 KiB for 570 KiB) in the Kubernetes ConfigMap portal-manual, with the page's sha256 and the commit it came from as annotations, and the portal's nginx sends it compressed.

After a change to the manual (a chapter edited, then python3 docs/manual/build.py and a commit), publish it:

  1. ./medcea.sh → Infrastructure → Publish the manual to the portal (it runs ./infra/publish-manual.sh, which takes the deploy lock and writes logs/publish-manual-<time>.log; it publishes the manual and nothing else).
  2. It prints the page's size, the size in the ConfigMap, the sha256 and the commit, restarts the portal (a few seconds) and ends "the portal serves it at /manual/". On an install whose portal is older than the manual (deployed before 3 November 2026), it only stores the manual and says the portal is not set up to serve it yet, without restarting it: run ./deploy-infra.sh once, which adds the /manual/ route, the mount and the card.
  3. ./health-check.sh: Platform manual is OK.

./deploy-infra.sh publishes the manual too, every run, before it updates the portal page. Both refuse, and the portal keeps the copy it has, when build.py refuses the chapters (a dead link, a duplicate id, a script; the message names the chapter) or when the compressed page would not fit in a ConfigMap (1 MiB at most; the limit used is 1,000,000 bytes). deploy-infra.sh stops there with an error, before the portal changes: fix the chapter and run it again.

The health check's Platform manual (type manual) rebuilds the page into a temporary file and compares it with what the ConfigMap holds. OK when they are the same; WARN when the portal serves an older build ("the portal serves the manual of <commit> …, the repository builds …", with the medcea.sh entry to run), when nothing is published yet, or when the portal does not mount the manual (run ./deploy-infra.sh); FAIL when build.py refuses the chapters, or when the ConfigMap's content is not the page its annotation names (someone changed it by hand: publish again); SKIP before the portal exists.

The ConfigMap is the portal's, like the portal's web server configuration (k8s/portal/nginx.conf, ConfigMap portal-nginx); ./apps/frontend/deploy.sh adds only the background image's folder to the portal. ./deploy-infra.sh --reset removes them with the namespace, and the next ./deploy-infra.sh publishes again.

Superset

Apache Superset 6.1.0 (apps/superset/) is the data analysis tool decided on 4 November 2026 (see Superset for what people see). Its code arrived on 6 November 2026 (stage B) without its access policy. Stage C (7 and 8 November 2026) added the policy: Superset's host, its resource group analysis and its database account svc_superset as a skeleton version (version 15 on the previous install), and the cells for its builders and viewers as a change version (version 16), both approved by qa and applied with ./apps/iam/apply.sh; Superset was installed on 8 November 2026 (decision record "Superset stage C", exercise E27). The factory file carries both, so a fresh install's version 1 has Superset, and since 8 November 2026 a fresh install installs it (decision record "Superset installed by default", exercise E28).

The first part of stage C, the wiring around Superset, was deployed before the policy and stays off wherever the applied policy gives no role a Superset setting. Every ./deploy-infra.sh creates the Keycloak client superset (callback https://superset.<domain>/oauth-authorized/keycloak, the groups scope, the two sign-out return addresses below) and writes its secret into config.env as SUPERSET_CLIENT_SECRET (read back from Keycloak, never rotated, never on a command line), and superset.<domain> joins the platform certificate, the server's hosts block and the alias redirects. A client no deployed app uses is inert.

When it is skipped. There is no switch of its own to turn Superset on. ./deploy-apps.sh --all (and so ./install.sh) runs ./apps/superset/deploy.sh on every install, and it installs nothing, prints one line and exits 0 while:

  • the applied access policy has no Superset tool, or has it but gives no role a setting yet (between the skeleton version and the change version of stage C): [superset] skipped: Superset is not in the applied access policy, or no role is given a setting;
  • IAM_GATES is false: "skipped: IAM_GATES=false, and Superset has no pre-policy sign-in" (Superset has no sign-in from before the access policy);
  • IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is not true, as with a config.env from before 8 November 2026 (a new one has it true): [superset] skipped: Superset needs IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=true (its data connection is svc_superset). Superset's data connection logs in only as svc_superset, never as the database superuser, and that account can log in only under this switch. ./install.sh then ends with "Still to do: Superset was skipped, it needs IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=true." and names the medcea.sh entry that turns it on; afterwards run ./apps/superset/deploy.sh;
  • no version of the access policy is applied yet (since 8 November 2026; the full deploy only): [superset] skipped: no version of the access policy is applied yet (state empty), and Superset deploys only from an applied one: run ./apps/superset/deploy.sh once ./apps/iam/deploy.sh has applied version 1 (./apps/iam/apply.sh --status). On a fresh install the iam deploy, which runs before it, applies version 1; this skip shows only when that bootstrap waited (the iam deploy warns why). Nothing deploys Superset again after a later bootstrap, so ./install.sh ends with "Still to do: Superset was skipped, no version of the access policy is applied yet. Once ./apps/iam/deploy.sh has applied version 1 (./apps/iam/apply.sh --status), run ./apps/superset/deploy.sh." A policy state that cannot be read, or any other state, stops the deploy (exit 1) instead.

In each case a Superset that is running is stopped: its Deployment is deleted, its portal card greyed out, and its database, Secret and ConfigMap are kept. With IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES true but svc_superset unable to log in (no password, no Secret db-svc-superset: ./apps/database/deploy.sh has not run since the skeleton version) the deploy is not skipped: it stops with an error. A policy that does not compile also stops it (exit 1), and any option other than --gate-only is refused (exit 2). Exercise E24 checks the skip.

Once the policy gives roles a setting, the same command installs it, in this order:

  1. The wheel cache (SUPERSET_WHEEL_DIR, below): any of the three pinned packages missing there is downloaded first, before anything the running Superset reads changes, so a failed download leaves it as it was.
  2. Superset's own database superset, owned by the login role superset_meta, created in the PostgreSQL pod (the password goes in only as a verifier, on standard input, in a session that logs no statement). It is outside the platform database medcea_db, as Keycloak's is, and the database deploy never compiles it.
  3. The Kubernetes Secret superset-secrets (the secret key, superset_meta's password, Superset's Keycloak client secret and the compiled role mapping) and the ConfigMap superset-config (Superset's settings and the MedCEA sign-in code).
  4. A one-off Job superset-init: Superset's own schema, its built-in roles, the role "MedCEA Viewer" and the connection MedCEA, logged in as svc_superset, with data changes, table creation, file upload and impersonation stated off and checked after saving. The deploy refuses unless the connection would log in as svc_superset (that needs IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES=true and ./apps/database/deploy.sh); it never uses the database superuser.
  5. The web Deployment superset, its Service and its address https://superset.<domain> (SUPERSET_DOMAIN), then the portal card is turned on.

The wheel cache. The Superset image is pinned by digest. It lacks the PostgreSQL driver and the sign-in library, so at every start an init container installs exactly three packages (psycopg2-binary, Authlib, joserfc), each checked against the SHA-256 in apps/superset/requirements.txt. Since stage C (decision N10) they come from a folder on the host, SUPERSET_WHEEL_DIR in config.env (empty: /var/lib/<project>/superset-wheels), mounted read-only, with no package index: a restart, by apply.sh's rollout, a reboot or an eviction, needs no internet. Since 8 November 2026 ./deploy-infra.sh creates the folder after the MicroK8s bootstrap and the Docker Hub registry setup, just before the Helm registry login ("Superset's wheel cache folder..."): mode 700, owned by the deploying account, with one sudo prompt that says why ("[sudo] password for <you> (to create … for Superset's wheels):") when the parent is not writable, so the applications stage, and an unattended ./deploy-apps.sh, need no sudo for it. It checks the folder against the volumes' directory with the same code the Superset deploy uses and stops on a folder inside or around it; run as root it creates nothing and says so; it creates the folder whether or not Superset is installed (an empty folder). The full Superset deploy still creates the folder when it is missing (asking for sudo itself) and refuses one owned by another account or by root, one inside or around the volumes' directory, and a run as root; when a package is missing it runs a one-off Job superset-wheels, which downloads it from PyPI (pip download --require-hashes, binary packages only) and is deleted once the cache is complete. A changed pin in requirements.txt therefore needs a full deploy with PyPI reachable, and so does the first install: the pods must reach pypi.org, not only the image registries. ./apps/superset/uninstall.sh keeps the folder; ./install.sh --uninstall-all removes it (see Uninstalling).

There is no Redis and no background worker: SQL Lab runs queries directly, and alerts, reports and thumbnails are off. A pod restart ends nobody's session; sessions last 5 minutes idle and at most one hour.

Sign-out. Superset's Logout ends Superset's session and sends the person to Keycloak's end-session, which returns to the AI Workbench's /hub/logout when WORKBENCH_ENABLED is true and to the portal's sign-out otherwise (decision N4; the pod's MEDCEA_LOGOUT_RETURN, an https address or Superset does not start). ./deploy-infra.sh registers both addresses on the client whatever WORKBENCH_ENABLED says.

./apps/superset/deploy.sh --gate-only checks only who may sign in, and never downloads:

  • not deployed while Superset does not run;
  • unchanged when the Secret holds the compiled role mapping and every running pod was started with the Secret and ConfigMap as they are now (the pods read the mapping only at start, so a Secret rewritten by a re-render that did not finish counts as drift);
  • re-rendered (role mapping): the Secret and ConfigMap are rewritten and Superset restarts from the wheel cache;
  • re-rendered (stopped, …): the applied policy no longer gives any role a setting, IAM_GATES is false or IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is not true; Superset is stopped and its card greyed out, as in the full deploy;
  • deferred, exit 4, when the mapping drifted while the wheel cache is incomplete and the running Superset admits only roles the policy still gives, in the same way (the policy only adds roles): Superset keeps its old mapping, apply.sh records apply_deferred ("Superset's wheel cache is incomplete"), and you run ./apps/superset/deploy.sh (it fills the cache), then ./apps/iam/apply.sh --resume --by <you>. Any other drift with an incomplete cache (a narrowing, a role mapped differently, a pod on another configuration) stops Superset instead: a mapping that would narrow is never deferred.

Either way Superset is closed, never left open, and the next ./deploy-infra.sh leaves a stopped Superset's card grey. apply.sh runs ./apps/superset/deploy.sh --gate-only in the rollout of every version from stage C's wiring on, whatever the version; it prints not deployed until Superset is installed.

Settings. ./infra/configure.sh generates three values once, before it checks for missing settings, and never asks or shows them: SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY (64 hex characters; it signs Superset's session cookies and encrypts the stored connection password, so changing it signs everyone out and the next deploy writes the connection again), SUPERSET_META_DB_PASS and SVC_SUPERSET_DB_PASS (it reaches the database, and Secret db-svc-superset, with the first ./apps/database/deploy.sh after the skeleton version that adds svc_superset). SUPERSET_CLIENT_SECRET is written by ./deploy-infra.sh (above). A rotated SVC_SUPERSET_DB_PASS needs ./apps/database/deploy.sh and then the full ./apps/superset/deploy.sh; a new SUPERSET_CLIENT_SECRET (regenerated in Keycloak, then ./deploy-infra.sh) needs the full deploy too: --gate-only compares the running Superset with the cluster's Secret, not with config.env.

Stage C, in order, as it was done on the previous install on 7 and 8 November 2026 (an install whose applied policy predates Superset follows the same path). Best through ./medcea.sh, which holds the deploy lock for each group of commands (exercise E27 walks through it):

  1. The wiring: ./deploy-infra.sh (client superset, the certificate name; run it with no onboarding or run active, since the certificate change reloads the ingress), ./apps/iam/deploy.sh (iam-api restarts: its compiler changed), ./deploy-apps.sh --all (Superset skipped), ./health-check.sh (Superset roles SKIP).
  2. The skeleton version: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by <you> --reason "<why>" --from-git <commit>, approved by a qa person with the attestation, then git checkout <commit> and ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <you>. Between that checkout and the end of the apply every deploy that compiles the policy exits 2 (the skeleton gate): run nothing else in between. Its rollout prints Superset not deployed.
  3. ./medcea.sh → Policy → Superset stage C: after the skeleton version: ./apps/database/deploy.sh (svc_superset's password and Secret), ./apps/iam/deploy.sh (the Access Policy then ships the new skeleton), the health check. Draft the change version only after this: the Access Policy checks a draft against the skeleton its own pod ships.
  4. The change version with the cells: drafted by an admin in the Access Policy, approved by qa, applied with ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <you>; its rollout still prints not deployed.
  5. ./medcea.sh → Policy → Superset stage C: install Superset: ./apps/superset/deploy.sh (the first install: the image, the wheels, the init Job), the health check, tests/iam-hosts.sh, tests/iam-network.sh, tests/iam-signin.sh and a backup (backups.sh now, then verify, which lists db/superset.dump).

./medcea.sh → Applications also has Install Superset (the deploy and the health check), Re-render Superset's gate (--gate-only) and Uninstall Superset (the word yes, and for --purge-data also the project name); Policy → Re-render the policy artefacts includes Superset's --gate-only.

Taking stage C back out.

  • The wiring (commit A): revert it in git, then ./deploy-infra.sh and ./apps/iam/deploy.sh. The Keycloak client superset stays behind, inert, since no deployed app uses it.
  • The skeleton version, proposed or approved but not applied: withdraw it (./apps/iam/apply.sh --withdraw-open, or qa returns it) and check out the wiring's commit again.
  • The skeleton version, applied: never reverted. Without the change version Superset never deploys.
  • The change version, applied: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --rollback-to <skeleton version> --by <you> --reason "…", then qa confirms it. Its rollout's --gate-only stops Superset and greys out its card, without needing PyPI; Superset's database is kept.
  • An IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES rollback stops Superset too (the deploy and --gate-only); no Superset pod ever runs on the database superuser.
  • Retiring Superset for good: a change version without the cells, then a commit that removes the group analysis and the host (a narrowing, which the next deploy accepts), then ./apps/superset/uninstall.sh. Leave svc_superset and Superset's network policy in place: removing either is a widening and would need its own skeleton version.

Superset users left by the sign-in test. Each sign-in creates a Superset user. tests/iam-signin.sh deactivates the ones its own run made (test-<role>-<run>) when it ends, in Superset's database as the database superuser, and does not delete them (decision N7). A run that was killed leaves its users active, though their Keycloak accounts are gone, so they cannot sign in. A username used again later finds its old Superset user, with what it owned.

Removing it. ./apps/superset/uninstall.sh greys out the card and removes everything labelled app=superset (Deployment, Jobs, Service, Ingress, Secret, ConfigMaps, a leftover superset-wheels Job included) and keeps the database superset and the wheel cache. ./apps/superset/uninstall.sh --purge-data also drops the database and the role superset_meta: every dashboard, chart, saved query and Superset account is gone. That flag is the only way to drop it. Neither touches svc_superset (the database deploy's) nor the platform database.

The deploy and uninstall write logs/app-superset-deploy-<time>.log and logs/app-superset-uninstall-<time>.log. Superset keeps its own log of sign-ins and actions in its database; Keycloak records each sign-in (login events of realm medcea). The health check's supersetroles (The health check) compares the running sign-in with the policy, and the running pods with the live Secret and ConfigMap; it is one of the ten checks apply.sh runs before and after an apply. Once Superset runs, tests/iam-hosts.sh checks its secrets, gate, running configuration, sign-in and reach, tests/iam-network.sh that no pod reaches it directly, and tests/iam-signin.sh who gets in.

Uninstalling

There are three levels, all through install.sh. Each lists what it removes and asks you to type a word to confirm, and refuses without a terminal.

CommandRemovesKeeps
./install.sh --uninstall-apps [component …] (type apps)All application components, or the ones named, each through its own apps/<component>/uninstall.sh.The infrastructure and the database contents.
./install.sh --uninstall-infra (type reset)Every platform service, every application and all data in the namespace: the database, Keycloak users, Grafana's volume (the dashboards Editors made in the browser), workbench home folders.MicroK8s (so a reinstall is fast), config.env, the platform CA, the backups in BACKUP_DIR.
./install.sh --uninstall-all (type uninstall)All of the above plus MicroK8s, the onboarding wizard service, edge/.venv, Superset's wheel cache (SUPERSET_WHEEL_DIR: only its wheels are deleted, so a folder holding anything else is kept and named; then /var/lib/<project> when it is left empty; sudo asked when needed), the MedCEA block in /etc/hosts, logs/ and the credentials files. Asks separately about config.env (with medcea.sh's backups) and the platform CA .ca/; the default is to keep them.edge/provisioned/ (the board provisioning records), edge/firmware/ and the backups in BACKUP_DIR. Tailscale and installed packages are not touched.

The infrastructure levels map to ./deploy-infra.sh --reset and ./deploy-infra.sh --uninstall. ./deploy-infra.sh --reset --secrets also blanks the generated credentials in config.env.

AI workbench home folders

Each person's workbench files live in their own volume, claim-<username>, in the namespace the workbench runs in (the research namespace after Phase 2b's move; the list below names both). Homes the move copied are kept on the host even after their claim goes ("kept on this host after the claim goes (Retain): remove its directory by hand when no longer needed"), and an old home the move left behind is listed as "left behind by the move to <namespace> (the copy there is the live one)". Stopping a workspace, removing a person from the hub, a role that loses the workbench, WORKBENCH_ENABLED=false and every workbench redeploy keep it. Only the nightly backup copies it (Backup and restore), and deleting the namespace or MicroK8s deletes it: --uninstall-infra, --uninstall-all, ./deploy-infra.sh --reset and --uninstall, and answering yes to "Fully wipe MicroK8s and reinstall?", which ./deploy-infra.sh asks when MicroK8s is installed but not fully up. Before they ask you to confirm, these list each home with the directory that holds it on the host, for example:

AI workbench homes that this deletes (newest nightly backup: 20261102-023000Z in /var/backups/medcea, which this keeps):
  - bio1: claim-bio1 (10Gi), on this host in /var/snap/microk8s/common/default-storage/medcea-claim-bio1-pvc-…

When no complete backup is found the line says "nothing backs them up" instead. To keep them, restore them from the nightly backup after the reinstall, or answer no, then either have each person commit and push their notebooks to the research repository (Saving your notebooks to git), or copy each listed directory off the volume with sudo cp -a <directory> ~/workbench-homes-backup/.
