E34 Two sensors on one reading in the Monitor and Grafana

Goal. See that two sensors publishing the same reading stay two series: the SHT45 and the SCD30 of the bench board both publish air_temperature and air_humidity, each on its own topic, and the Run Monitor and Grafana show one value or line per sensor. The exercise proves feedback control Phase 1 (see SENSE and CONTROL boards) and the decisions "Feedback control Phases 1 and 2: the owner's earlier answers" (Q13, D2) and "… deviations from the plan" (the Monitor per zone, reading and sensor; Grafana every sensor) in the decision record.

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer) in the onboarding wizard, the MQTT Explorer and Grafana; qa_user (qa) in the Run Monitor and Grafana (Viewer). No separation of duties is exercised.

Before you start.

  • The rollout of Phases 1 and 2 has reached at least its database, Monitor, report and wizard deploys (Rollout of Phases 1 and 2, step 5). Note git log -1 --oneline.
  • The bench SENSE board of E25 (SHT45 on hub channel 7, SCD30 on channel 6), still flashed with the firmware from before 13 November 2026, in UNIT01 / ZONE01.
  • A run on UNIT01 that has not completed (running, scheduled or failed), so that the Run Monitor shows the unit's card. A scheduled run blocks E36's save: remove it afterwards.

Steps.

  1. qa_user: open the Run Monitor and look at the unit's Live Measurements. Open Grafana's IoT Environmental Monitoring, last 15 minutes.
  2. eng: onboard the SENSE board again into UNIT01 / ZONE01 (Onboarding from the browser). At How is this board wired? choose Start from a saved board: Sense board as bench-tested 6 Nov 2026 …, then click the SCD30 and look at Published as. If the run shows Control loops, choose Decide later (E36 covers it). Let the run finish.
  3. eng: open the MQTT Explorer and watch medcea/UNIT01/ZONE01/sense for two minutes.
  4. qa_user: refresh the Run Monitor, and Grafana's dashboard.
  5. eng: in Grafana's Explore: SELECT msg->>'tag' AS tag, coalesce(msg->>'sensor', '(none)') AS sensor, count(*) FROM medcea.measurement WHERE device_dns = 'unit01-s-zone01' AND measure_timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2.

What you should see.

  • Step 1 (the old firmware): one Air Temp and one Humidity gauge without a sensor name; Grafana's gauges and lines are labelled "ZONE01 / default".
  • Step 2: the SCD30's co2, air_temperature and air_humidity are all ticked, and the findings list is empty: two sensors on one reading are allowed. The run's summary lists the topics with the sensor (…/sense/<tag>/<sensor>).
  • Step 3: …/sense/air_temperature/sht45_1, …/sense/air_temperature/scd30_1, …/sense/air_humidity/sht45_1, …/sense/air_humidity/scd30_1 and …/sense/co2/scd30_1, each message with "sensor"; _health and _test on their own topics, without a sensor.
  • Step 4: the Monitor shows "Air Temp · scd30_1", "Air Temp · sht45_1", "Humidity · scd30_1", "Humidity · sht45_1" and "CO₂ · scd30_1"; the old board's last readings stay beside them as "Air Temp · default" and "Humidity · default", dimmed with "last …" once they are older than 10 minutes. Grafana shows one gauge and one line per zone and sensor ("ZONE01 / sht45_1", "ZONE01 / scd30_1"), with the old "ZONE01 / default" line ending where the board was onboarded, and the summary table has a Sensor column with the latest values.
  • Step 5: rows for sht45_1 and scd30_1 on air_temperature and air_humidity, scd30_1 on co2, and (none) only on _health and _test.

Each reading is a row of medcea.measurement (type AP) with "sensor" in its message; the views medcea.msg_actual_points and medcea.v_ap_measurements show it in their sensor column (default for a message without one). The onboarding is recorded as in E25; the provisioning record edge/provisioned/unit01-s-zone01.json now holds the SCD30's three tags. Write the date, the commit and what each screen showed under Last done.

Refusals worth trying (on the wiring screen, step 2; undo each):

  • The SCD30's humidity renamed to air_temperature, its temperature already there: "scd30_1 already publishes temperature as air_temperature: one sensor cannot publish two readings on one tag."
  • A sensor's id set to default (with --wiring FILE on the host, since the screen gives ids itself): "default is reserved: the platform calls the sensor of a reading that names none "default". Give this sensor another id."

Afterwards. Keep the board. Remove the run you created only for this exercise (Scheduler).

Last done. Not yet run (written 13 November 2026, before the rollout of Phases 1 and 2).

E35 The runner's default map, fallback and alarms

Goal. See what a run does with a zone's control loops: a zone without loops runs on the default map and, with two sensors on a reading, gets no data and the alarm ambiguous_source rather than a guess; once a reference and a fallback are chosen, unplugging the reference hands over to the fallback with an alarm; with no fresh reading the loop holds its last command. The exercise proves the decisions "the reference sensor is always the person's choice" (Q20) and "the owner's earlier answers" (Q8, Q11) in the decision record; the behaviour is in Control loops.

Accounts and roles. A production_manager account to start and stop the run (make one with E1 if none exists); eng (engineer) to choose the loops between the two runs and to read the run log; the host operator for the health check.

Before you start.

  • The whole rollout of Phases 1 and 2 is done (Rollout of Phases 1 and 2), and UNIT01 / ZONE01 holds the bench SENSE board as after E34 and an onboarded CONTROL board (E22).
  • ZONE01 has no control loops yet (a new zone, or Stop all loops in E36). An approved recipe allowed on UNIT01 whose first step has air temperature, humidity and CO2 limits and no substrate temperature limits, with a few short cycles.
  • The chamber has no plants in it: the run drives real equipment.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./health-check.sh; read the Control loops line.
  2. Production manager: in the Scheduler, Run Now on UNIT01 with that recipe, then execute it. Let it run three minutes.
  3. eng: open the run's log in the Scheduler (Full log). Then the production manager stops the run.
  4. eng: choose ZONE01's loops as in E36 steps 1 to 3: air temperature on sht45_1 with the fallback scd30_1.
  5. Production manager: a new run of the same recipe; after two minutes, unplug the SHT45's cable at the hub. Wait three minutes.
  6. Unplug the SCD30's cable too and wait two minutes; plug both back and wait two minutes. The production manager stops the run; eng reads its log.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: Control loops WARN: "1 zone(s) run on the default map (no control_loop rows; Q20): UNIT01/ZONE01; 1 of them with several sensors on a tag (no_data + ALARM ambiguous_source: choose the reference in onboarding): …".
  • Step 3: near the top "Control loops: default, 4 loop(s)" and "WARNING: DEFAULT_LOOP_MAP unit=UNIT01 zones=ZONE01 (…)"; once the sensors had time to report, "ALARM ambiguous_source unit=UNIT01 zone=ZONE01 loop=air_temperature sensors=…: choose the reference in onboarding", the same for air_humidity, each repeated every 300 seconds; the co2 loop controls on its only sensor and sends commands to control/co2; the substrate loop is inactive for the step ("WARNING zone ZONE01 loop substrate_temperature: the recipe line has no …: inactive").
  • Step 5: "Control loops: table, …" (or mixed); after the unplug, once the SHT45's last reading is older than the maximum age (90 seconds unless set), "ALARM fallback_in_use unit=UNIT01 zone=ZONE01 loop=air_temperature using=scd30_1 stale=sht45_1(…)", and the loop keeps controlling on the SCD30.
  • Step 6: "ALARM_CLEARED fallback_in_use …" then "ALARM no_fresh_data … (holding the last command …)": no new air temperature command is sent and the board keeps the last one; the fans are not switched off for lack of data. After plugging back, "ALARM_CLEARED no_fresh_data …".

The run log (Scheduler, the run's Full log) holds every ALARM, ALARM_CLEARED and WARNING line. Each cycle's run parameters carry the loops the run used (control_loops) and where they came from (control_loops_source: default for the first run, table or mixed for the second). The commands are CT rows of medcea.measurement, each naming its loop and the sensors used; the board's reports are SP rows. Write the date, the commit, the run numbers and the alarm lines under Last done, and the result in the decision record's rows.

Refusals worth trying.

  • While a run is running, eng tries to change ZONE01's loops (E36): no picker, the reason in words.
  • Not a refusal but worth seeing: in step 6, nothing turns the fans off; only the end of the run does (Phase 4 changes that).

Afterwards. Plug every sensor back. Leave ZONE01's loops as chosen, or stop them in the picker. A CO2 Q-learning state from before 13 November 2026 learnt the fans the wrong way round: have qa retire it (Control loops).

Last done. Not yet run (written 13 November 2026, before the rollout of Phases 1 and 2).

E36 Choose a zone's control loops, and the refusals

Goal. Choose which sensor each loop of a zone is controlled on, as an engineer, in the wizard's tile and in a terminal; see that with two sensors on a reading nothing is chosen for you; and see who and when the platform refuses. The exercise proves the decisions on Q19, Q20 and the choices D-b to D-d in the decision record; the picker is described in Control loops of a zone.

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer) chooses and saves; qa_user (qa) and, if one exists, a maintenance account are refused; a production_manager account schedules a run for the busy refusal; the host operator reads the record. The separation shown: only the engineer's role may change loops, and the database refuses during a run whoever asks.

Before you start. The whole rollout of Phases 1 and 2 is done, version 2c included (Rollout of Phases 1 and 2), with IAM_DB_ROLES=true. UNIT01 / ZONE01 holds the bench SENSE board as after E34 (SHT45 and SCD30) and a CONTROL board. No run on UNIT01 is running or scheduled.

Steps.

  1. eng: open https://onboard-device.<domain> and choose the tile Control loops of a zone. Choose UNIT01 / ZONE01.
  2. Look at the rows and the findings list without changing anything.
  3. For Air temperature choose on one sensor, the reference sht45_1 and the fallback scd30_1; for Air humidity mean of the ticked. Continue.
  4. eng, on the host: ./edge/flash-device.sh --loops-only --unit UNIT01 --zone ZONE01; sign in with the code; answer the menus to keep what was saved.
  5. Open the tile again, click Stop all loops and answer the question with Cancel; then click Decide later and continue.
  6. Host operator, read-only: ./medcea.sh → Edge devices → Choose a zone's control loops, answer the questions and decline at Run it? [y/N].

What you should see.

  • Step 1: "Zone UNIT01 / ZONE01" and, when the zone has no loops yet, "This zone has no control loops yet, so it runs on the default map: …".
  • Step 2: Air temperature and Air humidity in error: "air_temperature has 2 sensors (…): choose the one it controls on, or mean/min/max, or mark it not controlled", and the page does not continue; CO₂ on scd30_1, chosen for you, driving the CONTROL board's CO2 fan actuator; Substrate temperature cannot be ticked (no ground_temperature sensor).
  • Step 3: the page ends with the run's summary "control loops saved: created air_temperature, air_humidity, co2" (or the codes you kept).
  • Step 4: the same sign-in box as onboarding, the zone, one menu per reading with several sensors and a fallback question; then "control loops unchanged (…)" when you kept the same answers. No USB question, no erase.
  • Step 5: Cancel keeps the loops; Decide later saves nothing ("control loops: decided later").
  • Step 6: the command ./edge/flash-device.sh --loops-only --unit UNIT01 --zone ZONE01 and "the zone's medcea.control_loop rows (through save_zone_loops, as you); no board is touched", then nothing runs.

The saved loops are rows of medcea.control_loop, stamped with eng as creator and last changer, and each change is a row of medcea.row_change, which qa and auditor can export from Database Management with the audit histories. Nobody reads the table itself but the runner: opening the tile again shows what is saved, and the host operator may read it with psql in the PostgreSQL pod. A stop deactivates a row, never deletes it. Write the date, the commit, what was saved and each refusal's text under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • qa_user opens the tile: the wizard's page says that one of the onboarding roles is required to provision hardware, and offers no start. On the host, ./edge/flash-device.sh --loops-only signed in as qa_user stops right after the sign-in, naming those roles.
  • A maintenance account (if one exists) re-onboards the SENSE board: no picker; "maintenance does not choose control loops: an engineer does (./edge/flash-device.sh --loops-only --unit UNIT01 --zone ZONE01)". (Under IAM_DB_ROLES=true its registration is then refused too: a known gap.) Its --loops-only gets the same sentence and saves nothing.
  • The production manager schedules a run on UNIT01; eng opens the tile: "Unit UNIT01 has run … The loops of UNIT01 / ZONE01 change only while no run is running or scheduled, so this goes on and leaves them as they are." Remove the scheduled run.
  • Before version 2c is applied (only during the rollout): eng gets "your role (engineer) may not change control loops (engineer only), or policy version 2c is not applied yet".

Afterwards. Keep the loops for E35, or stop them (Stop all loops, confirmed) to give the zone back to the default map.

Last done. Not yet run (written 13 November 2026, before the rollout of Phases 1 and 2).

E37 A Fungi recipe with setpoints

Goal. Write a recipe of a recipe type, with one lower and upper limit per quantity of the type on each step; export it and import it again; see that a recipe runs only on units of its type and that an incomplete recipe cannot be approved. The exercise proves the decisions on recipe types, the setpoints map and the unit's type in the decision record; the screens are in Configuration UI.

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer) writes the recipe; a production_manager account assigns it; qa_user (qa) approves it. The separation shown: the engineer writes, the production manager plans, qa approves what someone else wrote.

Before you start. Migration 011 is deployed with the Configuration UI and the Run Monitor (Rollout of the recipe types). UNIT01 is a Fungi unit. For the refusals that the database decides, note whether IAM_DB_ROLES is true (refused) or still false during the build (a warning only).

Steps.

  1. eng: Recipes tab, + New Recipe, Name E37 Pleurotus test, Recipe Type Fungi, Save.
  2. Steps →, + Add Step: Step # 1, Cycles 1, light type DARK, 0 and 60 minutes; air temperature 20–24, air humidity 85–95; leave CO2 empty and try Save Step; then fill CO2 400–1200 and save.
  3. Open the recipe again and look at Recipe Type.
  4. ↓ Export the recipe; open the file in a text editor; ↑ Import it again (it becomes a second recipe with the same steps).
  5. Import an old file from the Platform Recipe Library (one of the Basilico files before 15 November 2026, or any file without recipe_type).
  6. Production manager: Units tab, Recipe ↔ Unit Permissions: look at the cell of the recipe and UNIT01, and at a Plants recipe's cell.
  7. qa_user: Approvals tab, approve E37 Pleurotus test.

What you should see.

  • Step 2: one lower and upper pair per quantity of the Fungi type, the required ones marked; the step is not saved while CO2 is empty; once saved, the step table's Setpoints column lists the three ranges.
  • Step 3: the field is greyed, "Fixed: the recipe has steps."
  • Step 4: the file has "format": 2, "recipe_type": "FUNGI" and each step's setpoints (the recipe file); the imported copy has the same steps.
  • Step 5: the import asks which recipe type it is, and the old limits arrive as setpoints.
  • Step 6: the Fungi recipe's cell can be ticked; the Plants recipe's cell on UNIT01 shows ≠, "a recipe runs only on units of its type".
  • Step 7: the approval is recorded and the recipe reads approved.

The step's limits are the setpoints of its row in medcea.recipe_line, and the recipe's type medcea.recipe.recipe_type; each change is a row of medcea.row_change with the person, and the approval a row of medcea.approval whose digest covers the setpoints. Write the date, the commit, the recipe and approval numbers and each refusal's text under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • A step with air humidity 80–120: refused by the form, and by the database ("recipe_line setpoints: air_humidity must be within 0 and 100 %RH").
  • A lower limit above the upper one: "recipe_line setpoints: … lower … is above upper …".
  • qa_user approves a recipe one of whose steps lacks a required quantity (an old step written before the form required it): "approve_recipe: recipe … misses required setpoints: line … lacks co2".
  • A Plants recipe assigned to UNIT01 or run on it through the API: under IAM_DB_ROLES=true refused with "recipe_type: recipe … is a PLANT recipe and unit UNIT01 a FUNGI unit"; while it is false it goes through, and the database's warning says "IAM_DB_ROLES=false, would refuse: recipe_type: …".
  • qa_user approves the recipe eng wrote, as eng: refused, the author rule (Drafts, approval and the author rule).

Afterwards. Retire the test recipes (Retire…), or keep one for E38's run.

Last done. 16 November 2026, partly, on commit bc75f69 (migrations 011 and 012). While enforcement was relaxed for the build, eng wrote two Fungi recipes in the Configuration UI: recipe 1 Test (one step, with air temperature, air humidity, CO2 and light intensity) and recipe 2 Pleurotus ostreatus v01.02 (three steps, with air temperature, air humidity, CO2 and substrate temperature); recipe 2 was permitted on UNIT01, and a run of it (run 1) failed at its start as expected, "No active actuator found for unit code: UNIT01" (no CONTROL board yet), its runner having read the steps' setpoints. Once full enforcement was back, qa_user approved recipe 2 in the Approvals tab (approval 7, 21:46 UTC, signed with qa_user's own token; author eng) and returned recipe 1 with the note "incomplete" (approval 6), which stays a draft. Steps 3 to 6 (the fixed type, export and import, an old file, the permission matrix's ≠) and the refusals were not run.

E38 Bind a zone's loops board by board

Goal. See that each board's onboarding binds its own half of the zone's control loops, in either order: the SENSE board the sensors, the CONTROL board the actuators; that a half-bound loop is shown as such and that a run uses the default map's other half meanwhile; and that --loops-only binds both. The exercise proves the decision on half-by-half binding and the implementation choice on half-bound loops in the decision record; the picker is in Control loops of a zone.

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer) onboards and chooses; the host operator reads the run log and the health check. The separation shown: only the engineer's role saves loops.

Before you start. The recipe types are deployed, with IAM_DB_ROLES=true (the picker needs it). UNIT01 / ZONE01 has its SENSE board (SHT45 and SCD30) and no saved loops; a CONTROL board is at hand for the zone. No run on UNIT01 is running or scheduled.

Steps.

  1. eng: re-onboard the SENSE board into UNIT01 / ZONE01 (or, with no board on the bench, the tile Control loops of a zone). At the Control loops step, choose sht45_1 for air temperature and air humidity, scd30_1 for CO2.
  2. Host operator: ./health-check.sh, the Control loops line.
  3. Host operator: start a short run of a Fungi recipe on UNIT01 and read the start of its run log; stop it.
  4. eng: onboard the CONTROL board into UNIT01 / ZONE01; at the Control loops step, look at the actuator chosen for each quantity and continue.
  5. eng: open the tile Control loops of a zone for UNIT01 / ZONE01.
  6. Host operator: ./health-check.sh again.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: "Which sensor does each loop control on?", one row per loop of the Fungi type, with no actuator question; when the zone has no CONTROL board, "no CONTROL board in UNIT01 / ZONE01 yet: the loops this board feeds wait for their actuators, chosen when the CONTROL board is onboarded".
  • Step 2: Control loops warns of half-bound loops, "… running on the default map's other half until its onboarding chooses it: UNIT01/ZONE01 air_humidity (no output); …".
  • Step 3: the run log has "WARNING: zone ZONE01: loop … is half-bound: its output is the default map's (actuator …) until a CONTROL onboarding chooses it".
  • Step 4: "Which actuator does each loop drive?", each actuator that declares a quantity already chosen for it; the sensors are not asked again.
  • Step 5: each row reads live.
  • Step 6: no half-bound warning.

Each half is written through medcea.save_zone_loops with eng's sign-in: the SENSE onboarding's save fills input, the CONTROL onboarding's output of the same medcea.control_loop row, and each is a row of medcea.row_change. The run's cycle records the loops it ran with, a half-bound one marked "completed". Write the date, the commit, what was bound in which order and each text under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • In the picker, choose for CO2 a sensor tag in another unit: "sensor … publishes … in …, not ppm".
  • For a CONTROL board whose fan actuator declares CO2, choose it for air humidity: "actuator … acts on co2, not air_humidity".
  • A loop for light intensity: not offered ("light_intensity: a setpoint only, without a feedback loop yet").

Afterwards. Keep the loops, or Stop all loops from --loops-only to give the zone back to the default map.

Last done. Not yet run. On 16 November 2026 the owner deferred it to the end of the plan, with the other deferred exercises; its first part needs no CONTROL board (./edge/flash-device.sh --loops-only --unit UNIT01 --zone ZONE01, as eng, with IAM_DB_ROLES=true).

E39 Run a controller comparison campaign

Goal. Run a small controller comparison campaign on the chamber model, with production's own controllers and loop rules, and check what makes it evidence: the same spec on the same code gives the same result digest; PID's result depends on the clock's origin; an FLC or MPC run that fell back to on/off control is marked invalid; and the campaign refuses what it cannot vouch for. The exercise proves the decisions "controller campaigns first" and "loosely coupled, data by snapshot only" in the decision record; the harness is described in Research sandbox.

Accounts and roles. The host operator runs the commands, on behalf of a control_scientist (no research role has any right before Phase 2, and Phase 1 is a command on the host: Not built yet). No platform account signs in; nothing on the platform changes.

Before you start. A clean checkout of the commit to test. Run the exercise in a worktree of it, never in the platform's own checkout, whose schd/ is the live runner's code: git worktree add ../medcea-e39 HEAD && cd ../medcea-e39. python3-venv installed and PyPI reachable (for step 4).

Steps.

  1. Check the contract sources and the sandbox are committed: git status --short -- schd/cea apps/database/recipe_types.yaml edge/templates/esp32-control.json research.
  2. Write the spec: one scenario, the five controllers, two seeds, three clock offsets. (The shipped research/harness/campaigns/smoke.yaml is a similar spec with small parameter grids; this one keeps every controller at its defaults so the lines compare.) 
    mkdir -p ~/e39 && cat > ~/e39/e39.yaml <<EOF
description: E39 controller comparison, smoke scenario
scenarios:
  - $PWD/research/harness/scenarios/smoke_air_temperature.yaml
controllers:
  - {code: IF_THEN_ELSE}
  - {code: PID}
  - {code: Q_LEARNING}
  - {code: FLC}
  - {code: MPC}
seeds: [1, 2]
clock_offsets_s: [0, 5, 9.99]
EOF
  3. Run it with the host's own Python: python3 -m research.harness.campaign ~/e39/e39.yaml --out ~/e39/host. No --allow-dirty: the worktree is a clean checkout.
  4. Build the virtual environment: source research/lib-venv.sh && ensure_research_venv.
  5. Run it in the virtual environment twice, the second time on one process: research/.venv/bin/python -m research.harness.campaign ~/e39/e39.yaml --out ~/e39/run1, then the same with --out ~/e39/run2 --jobs 1.
  6. Compare the digests: grep -h result_digest ~/e39/run1/manifest.json ~/e39/run2/manifest.json.
  7. Read the air temperature loop of every run (controller, seed, clock offset, valid, distance from the middle, time next to an edge, OFF commands, energy): 
    python3 -c 'import json, sys
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    r = json.loads(line); a = r["loops"]["air_temperature"]
    print(r["controller"]["code"], r["seed"], r["clock_offset_s"], r["valid"], round(a["rmsd_mid"], 3),
          a["boundary_hugging"], a["commands"]["UP"], a["commands"]["OFF"], round(r["energy_total_wh"], 1))' ~/e39/run1/results.jsonl
  8. Read ~/e39/run1/manifest.json: code.commit, code.dirty, code.blobs, code.controller_libraries, spec_digest, cpu_hours_estimate.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: nothing printed.
  • Step 3: "campaign: 30 runs (12 invalid), …". The 12 are every FLC and MPC run; in ~/e39/host/results.jsonl each says, for example, "MPC fell back to bang-bang on … of … computed ticks (gekko is not installed (No module named 'gekko'))", and its controller_messages hold the controller's own WARNING mpc fallback: … line.
  • Step 5: "campaign: 30 runs (0 invalid), …" both times; a run takes about a minute or two on the host (MPC solves an optimisation at every tick).
  • Step 6: the two result_digest values are the same.
  • Step 7: If-Then-Else, FLC, MPC and Q-learning give the same line at all three clock offsets of a seed; PID's lines differ with the offset, with more OFF commands at 9.99 than at 0 for the same seed (PID depends on the clock). If-Then-Else stays in the band but next to its lower edge (time next to an edge about 0.5, the most distance from the middle); MPC, starting 4 °C below the band, answers mostly UP and holds the air near the band's middle.
  • Step 8: dirty false, the commit you checked out, a blob hash for each controller module, loop_resolver.py, params.py, the catalogue, the CONTROL template, the migration file and every file of research/, contract_version 1, and "present": true for FLC and MPC.

Nothing is recorded on the platform: the campaign reads the repository and writes only ~/e39/. Its evidence is the folder itself: manifest.json (commit, blob hashes, libraries, spec digest, seeds, offsets, result digest) and results.jsonl. Write the date, the commit, the two digests, the number of invalid runs in each step and the refusal texts under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. Each exits 2 and writes no output folder.

  • A controller code that does not exist: change IF_THEN_ELSE to LQR in a copy of the spec. "campaign: unknown algorithm code 'LQR' (known: FLC, IF_THEN_ELSE, MPC, PID, Q_LEARNING)". Production's factory would silently run on/off control for it.
  • A changed contract source: touch schd/cea/algorithms/e39_probe.py in the worktree and run step 5 again. "campaign: the contract sources or the sandbox's code differ from HEAD (schd/cea/algorithms/e39_probe.py): commit them, or pass --allow-dirty (allow_dirty=True from Python) to record them as dirty". The same happens for a changed file under research/. Delete the file afterwards.
  • Over the CPU cap: step 5 with --max-cpu-hours 0.001. "campaign: estimated 0.11 CPU-hours for 30 runs, over the cap of 0.001 (--max-cpu-hours)" (the estimate is this host's, printed with three significant digits).
  • A parameter outside a controller's schema, for example {code: PID, params: {cycle_time: 0.5}}: refused with the schema's problem.

Afterwards. rm -r ~/e39 (keep the folder if the numbers are evidence for a proposal); leave the worktree with cd - and remove it with git worktree remove ../medcea-e39.

Last done. 17 November 2026, commit a175c52, in a worktree of it, by the host operator. Step 1: nothing printed. Step 3 (host Python 3.14): "campaign: 30 runs (12 invalid)", every FLC and MPC run, each MPC run "MPC fell back to bang-bang on 1079 of 1079 computed ticks (gekko is not installed (No module named 'gekko'))". Step 5: "30 runs (0 invalid)" both times; the first run took 1 min 12 s, the second with --jobs 1 6 min 42 s. Step 6: both result digests a96b20d15d6c57ba…. Step 7: If-Then-Else, FLC, MPC and Q-learning gave the same line at all three offsets of a seed; PID's distance from the middle and OFF commands moved with the offset (seed 1: 0.288 / 46 OFF at 0, 0.268 / 55 OFF at 9.99); If-Then-Else 1.60 from the middle with 0.49 of the time next to an edge, MPC 0.11 with 228 UP and none next to an edge, FLC 0.11, PID 0.27–0.31, Q-learning 1.91–1.94. Step 8: dirty false, 29 blob hashes, contract version 1, FLC and MPC present; estimate 0.116 CPU-hours. All four refusals exited 2 with the texts above and wrote no folder (the CPU estimate read 0.112).

E40 Controller libraries in the scheduler

Goal. See that the scheduler pod has the libraries MPC and FLC need, so that they run their own code rather than on/off control, and that MPC now drives a reading towards its band. The exercise proves the decision "MPC's command sign fixed and its libraries installed in the scheduler" in the decision record; the health check is in Control loops.

Accounts and roles. The host operator deploys and reads the health check and the run log; eng (engineer) writes an MPC parameter set or assignment for a test unit; qa_user (qa) approves it. The separation shown: choosing MPC for a unit is a configuration change a second person approves.

Before you start. No run is active or scheduled to start during the deploy (pgrep -af '[r]un_recipe.py' prints nothing). A test unit with a CONTROL and a SENSE board and nothing growing in it.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./apps/scheduler/deploy.sh.
  2. Host operator: ./health-check.sh, the Controller libraries line.
  3. eng: Configuration UI, Control Models, Parameter Sets, + New Parameter Set: Name E40 MPC test, Algorithm MPC, Unit the test unit, the default Params; Save draft. qa_user: Approvals tab, approve it. Then give the test unit's recipe assignment (or a schedule) that parameter set.
  4. Start a short run on the test unit with the air temperature below its band; follow the run log (Scheduler, the run's log) and the Run Monitor for a few minutes; stop the run.

What you should see.

  • Step 2: Controller libraries OK, "pod scheduler-…: gekko 1.3.3, scikit-fuzzy 0.5.0 (the pinned versions)".
  • Step 4: the run log has no line "WARNING mpc fallback"; the loop's command is UP while the reading is below the band, and the reading moves towards the band.

The parameter set is a row of medcea.unit_algorithm_params, each change a row of medcea.row_change and the approval a row of medcea.approval; the run records the parameter set it ran with (recipe_run.params_id). The health check's line is in logs/health-check-*.log. Write the date, the commit, the approval number, the health line and the first commands of the run under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • Run ./health-check.sh before step 1, on a scheduler pod started before the libraries were added: Controller libraries warns "gekko is not installed: MPC runs as bang-bang", and a run with MPC then has "WARNING mpc fallback: …" in its log.
  • A run with the parameter set before qa_user approved it: with IAM_DB_ROLES=true only an approved set runs (Approvals of configuration).

Afterwards. Set the test unit back to its previous algorithm (another draft, approved), or keep MPC if that is the plan for the unit.

Steps 1 and 2 on 17 November 2026, commit a175c52, with no run active: ./apps/scheduler/deploy.sh, then ./health-check.sh, all 66 checks OK, Controller libraries "pod scheduler-5c5fc958bd-rp95s: gekko 1.3.3, scikit-fuzzy 0.5.0 (the pinned versions)". In the pod, one MPC and one FLC built from production's own modules answered 18 °C → UP and 29 °C → DOWN for the band 22–25 °C with no fallback. E41 Pods left on the old AppArmor profile

Goal. See that ./deploy-infra.sh leaves containerd running, also when sudo is refused at its Docker Hub step, and that after a containerd restart Container AppArmor names the pods that keep MicroK8s's own profile, which a restart of each clears. The exercise proves the decision of 17 November 2026 "No containerd restart on a running cluster" (see the decision record).

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the OS account that deploys, with sudo). No platform account.

Before you start. The host runs a kernel from 7.0.0-41 with the rules installed (E29); ./health-check.sh passes. No onboarding run, recipe run or other deploy is active. Steps 1 to 3 need no more; the refusal at the end restarts containerd and is for a quiet moment.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: sudo -k, then ./deploy-infra.sh; at the prompt "[sudo] password for <you> (MicroK8s registry credentials):" type a wrong password three times.
  2. Host operator: journalctl -u snap.microk8s.daemon-containerd --since "-30 min" | grep -E 'Stopping|Started'.
  3. Host operator: ./deploy-infra.sh again, with the right password; then ./health-check.sh.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: after the three attempts, "WARNING: could not check or write …/certs.d/docker.io/hosts.toml (sudo refused or no credentials); left as it is. Nothing was restarted." and the deploy goes on (later steps that need sudo ask again).
  • Step 2: no Stopping or Started line from the deploy's time: containerd was not restarted.
  • Step 3: "Docker Hub credentials file for containerd..." then "Already in place — unchanged." (or, the first time after 17 November 2026 if the file differed, "Written (containerd reads it at the next pull; no restart)."); all checks OK.

Nothing is written to the policy history. The deploys are in logs/deploy-infra-<time>.log, the health check in logs/health-check-<time>.log, containerd's starts and the refused signals in the journal (journalctl -u snap.microk8s.daemon-containerd, journalctl -k -b | grep 'DENIED.*signal'), sudo's refusals in the auth log.

Refusals worth trying.

  • At a quiet moment, restart containerd by hand (sudo systemctl restart snap.microk8s.daemon-containerd), wait a few minutes, run ./health-check.sh: Container AppArmor FAILs "… signal denial(s) inside containers since the rules were loaded (…), sent from N pod(s) still running since before the rules were put back (a containerd restart): <kind>/<name> -n <namespace>, …; restart them (microk8s kubectl rollout restart <kind>/<name> -n <namespace>), then sudo systemctl start <project>-containerd-apparmor.service". Restart each as named (After a kernel update nothing starts, "After a containerd restart"), start the unit, run the health check again: OK. A pod that sends no signal is not named, although it may keep the old profile until its next restart.

Afterwards. Nothing to undo.

Last done. 18 November 2026, commit 53cc59a, by the host operator, no run active. Step 3 first (08:03 UTC, logs/deploy-infra-20261118-080332.log): "Already in place — unchanged."; ./health-check.sh at 08:09, all 66 checks OK. Step 1 (17:20 UTC, logs/deploy-infra-20261118-172002.log): after three wrong passwords, "WARNING: could not check or write /var/snap/microk8s/current/args/certs.d/docker.io/hosts.toml (sudo refused or no credentials); left as it is. Nothing was restarted."; the deploy finished. Step 2: no Stopping or Started line since 08:00. The health check after step 1 (17:24) failed one check, Container AppArmor: "1 signal denial(s) inside containers since the rules were loaded (Wed 2026-11-18 08:03:44 UTC), sent from 1 pod(s) still running since before the rules were put back (a containerd restart): deployment/hostpath-provisioner -n kube-system; restart it …". That pod is a leftover of the 17 November containerd restart (its process started on 16 November; its refused SIGURG came at 12:58 UTC, hours before step 1), not of these deploys: the naming of "Refusals worth trying" seen without a new restart. The refusal itself (a containerd restart by hand) not run.

E42 Hold out a range and export the first snapshot

Goal. A qa person holds a range of one unit's readings out of the research lake, the first nightly export then writes a snapshot without them, and the research zone admits nothing its policies do not compile. The exercise proves the decisions of 18 November 2026 on the research data (no person in it, read functions only, an append-only lake, the research database outside the policy matrix) in the decision record; the reference is Held-out reservations and The nightly export.

Accounts and roles. The host operator runs the commands; qa_user (qa) is the person named by --by, and is at the terminal for step 2 or has asked for that range in writing. eng (engineer) is the account a refusal names. The separation shown: only qa holds data out, and the export's login reads only what the read functions return.

Before you start.

  • The second commit of research Phase 2a (the research zone and svc_research_export in the access policy) is applied as a skeleton version: proposed with ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --from-git <commit> --by admin --reason "…", approved by qa_user in the Access Policy with the attestation, applied with ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by admin (apply.sh).
  • RESEARCH_ENABLED=true and the enable recipe run: ./medcea.sh → Infrastructure → Turn the research sandbox on or off. It runs ./deploy-infra.sh, ./apps/database/deploy.sh, ./apps/research/deploy.sh, ./apps/backup/deploy.sh and ./apps/research-export/deploy.sh under one lock. IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is true.
  • No export has run yet (the health check's Research export says "no snapshot yet"), so the range below is not in the lake. Pick a six-hour range of a day on which UNIT01 published readings, in the past.

Steps.

  1. Host operator: ./apps/research/reserve.sh list.
  2. Host operator, for qa_user: ./apps/research/reserve.sh add --by qa_user --unit UNIT01 --from 2026-11-15T00:00Z --to 2026-11-15T06:00Z --reason "E42: held out for the final validation"; read the summary and type yes.
  3. Host operator: ./apps/research/reserve.sh list again.
  4. Host operator: microk8s kubectl -n medcea create job --from=cronjob/research-export research-export-now-1, wait until microk8s kubectl -n medcea get job research-export-now-1 shows it complete, then microk8s kubectl -n medcea logs job/research-export-now-1.
  5. Host operator, read-only, in the research database: 
    microk8s kubectl exec -i -n medcea-research research-postgresql-0 -- sh -c 'PGPASSWORD="$(cat "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE")" exec psql -X -U postgres -d medcea_research' <<'SQL'
SELECT snapshot_id, cut_at, contract_version, rows FROM lake.snapshot ORDER BY snapshot_id;
SELECT count(*) FROM lake.measurement WHERE lower(unit_code) = 'unit01'
   AND measured_at >= '2026-11-15T00:00Z' AND measured_at < '2026-11-15T06:00Z';
SQL
  6. Host operator: ./health-check.sh, the lines Research network policies and Research export.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: "No reservations: nothing is held out of the research lake."
  • Step 2: the summary (unit, zone "(every zone)", from, to, reason, by qa_user and its account id) and "This cannot be changed or removed afterwards."; after yes, "Reservation #1 made: unit UNIT01 [2026-11-15T00:00Z, 2026-11-15T06:00Z) is held out of every snapshot from now on (apps/research/reserve.sh list)."
  • Step 3: one row under ID, UNIT, ZONE, FROM, TO, BY, MADE, REASON, with ZONE *.
  • Step 4: "research-export: no snapshot yet: this one starts from the beginning", "research-export: cut …, contract version 1", "research-export: snapshot 1 cut … measurements M" (M counts every reading read, the held-out ones included).
  • Step 5: one snapshot, contract version 1, whose rows has a held_out count above 0 and measurement equal to M minus it; the count of readings in the range is 0.
  • Step 6: Research network policies OK "3 research NetworkPolicies, the compiled set (default deny included)"; Research export OK "newest snapshot 0 h old (snapshot 1, no reserved rows in it);1 reservation(s)"; 68 checks.

The reservation is a row of vault.reservation in the research database (unit, zone, range, reason, by_username, by_sub, created_at), the snapshot a row of lake.snapshot (cut, previous cut, contract version, row counts with held_out, sha256 digests). Neither is on the policy history: the research database is outside the policy matrix. The commands log to logs/app-research-reserve-<time>.log and logs/health-check-<time>.log; the export's line is in the Job's log, kept for the last three runs. Write the date, the commit, the applied version, the reservation number, the snapshot number with its rows, and the two health lines under Last done.

Refusals worth trying.

  • A reservation of exported data: after step 4, step 2 again for a range of UNIT01 that the snapshot does hold, such as the day before (--from 2026-11-14T00:00Z --to 2026-11-14T06:00Z, a day with readings): "Refused by the research database: reserve: unit UNIT01 (every zone) from … to … is already exported: it is no longer held out. Nothing was written."
  • Someone who is not qa: ./apps/research/reserve.sh add --by eng --unit UNIT01 --from 2026-12-01 --to 2026-12-02 --reason "E42 refusal test": "--by eng does not hold the realm role qa: only qa reserves held-out data." Nothing is asked or written.
  • The research zone reaching the platform's database: microk8s kubectl exec -n medcea-research research-postgresql-0 -- timeout 5 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/rdbms-postgresql.medcea.svc.cluster.local/5432'; echo $?. The name resolves (DNS is allowed), the connection does not: after 5 seconds the exit code is 124. Nothing in the research namespace may open a connection the compile does not list.
  • A policy the zone did not compile: microk8s kubectl -n medcea-research create -f - with a NetworkPolicy e42-allow-all (empty pod selector, ingress: [{}]), then ./health-check.sh: Research network policies FAILs "not the zone's, no medcea/rs-netpol=true label: e42-allow-all, which widens the zone past its default deny …". Delete it at once (microk8s kubectl delete networkpolicy -n medcea-research e42-allow-all).

Afterwards. The reservation stays: it cannot be removed, and it is what the final validation will use. A reservation made only for this exercise is recorded as such by its reason. The CronJob goes on every night at 03:00 UTC; the Job made by hand is removed with the older ones.

E43 Move the AI Workbench into the research zone and read a snapshot

Goal. Apply research Phase 2b's skeleton version, move the AI Workbench into the research zone, and show that a notebook there reads the newest snapshot with its provenance and reaches nothing of the platform. The exercise proves the decisions of 19 November 2026 in the decision record: the switchover under one lock, the reader with no identity (O2), the hub without Secrets under pod security baseline, the internet on TCP 443 only, and D1 = A2 (the hub administrator gets no workspace, invariant I19); the reference is The AI Workbench in the research zone, Reading snapshots from a notebook and Moving the AI workbench.

Accounts and roles. The host operator runs the commands. admin (admin, the hub administrator) proposes the skeleton version and applies it; qa_user (qa) approves it. A scientist test account, for example bio_test (bio_scientist, made with E1 and listed in the test accounts), opens the notebook. The separation shown: the administrator administers the hub but works in no workspace; a scientist works on snapshots only.

Before you start.

  • Research Phase 2b's first commit is deployed (./deploy-infra.sh, ./deploy-apps.sh --all) and ./health-check.sh shows 71 checks with Research lake reader SKIP. RESEARCH_ENABLED is true and at least one snapshot exists (E42).
  • The engineer's Superset dashboards are exported, and a backup was taken after the approval (./apps/backup/backups.sh now).
  • No notebook server runs (the hub's admin page lists none running). bio_test has used the workbench before the move, so it has a home to carry, holding one file you can recognise, for example e43-before.txt.
  • Use one browser session per account (running an exercise safely).

Steps.

  1. admin, on the host: ./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by admin --reason "Research Phase 2b: the AI Workbench in the research zone" --from-git <commit B>, first with --check-only. qa_user: approve the version in the Access Policy's Approval tab with the attestation.
  2. Host operator: check out commit B, then ./medcea.sh → Policy → Research Phase 2b: apply the skeleton version and move the workbench. Give the version number and --by admin; confirm; at the move's question type yes; give the sudo password when it asks "to copy the home claim-bio_test into medcea-research".
  3. Host operator: microk8s kubectl -n medcea-research get pods,pvc, microk8s kubectl -n medcea get pvc -l medcea/moved-to=medcea-research, and microk8s kubectl get rolebinding,role -n medcea-research.
  4. bio_test: open the AI Workbench from the portal, wait for JupyterLab, check that e43-before.txt is there, open medcea-examples/01-connect.ipynb and run it; then 02-air-temperature.ipynb.
  5. bio_test: in a new cell, df = md.measurements("UNIT01", "ZONE01", minutes=120) and md.provenance(df).
  6. Host operator: tests/iam-research.sh.
  7. admin: on the hub's admin page, list the users, then try to start a server of your own (Start My Server).
  8. Host operator: ./deploy-infra.sh, then ./health-check.sh, and read Keycloak client scopes, AI Workbench gate, Workbench accounts, Research grants and Secrets, Research lake reader and Research network policies.

What you should see.

  • Step 2: the apply ends with the workbench deferred ("the AI workbench moves into the research zone"); the move lists the volumes set to Retain, says workbench-notebook: disabled, copies claim-bio_test (and every other home but claim-admin, which it names), installs the workbench, and prints what is left and how to remove it; lake-api deploys; --resume closes the deferral; the health check passes.
  • Step 3: hub, proxy and lake-api pods Running in medcea-research; claim-bio_test Bound there; the old claim-bio_test in medcea still Bound with the label; Role medcea-hub, whose rules name no secrets.
  • Step 4: the file is there; md.connect() prints one line with the newest snapshot's number, cut, contract version 1 and lineage, and asks for no sign-in; the chart's title names the snapshot.
  • Step 5: a table whose newest reading is at or before the snapshot's cut, with ingested_at and snapshot_id columns; the provenance holds the snapshot, its lineage with lineage_verified true, the set digest and response_sha256.
  • Step 6: every platform target timed out (configuration API, broker, both databases, scheduler, ingress, the host's addresses), lake-api and one internet host on 443 reached.
  • Step 7: the admin page works; starting a server of your own is refused: "Administration of the AI workbench gives no workspace: sign in with an account whose role uses the workbench."
  • Step 8: Keycloak client scopes OK with workbench-notebook disabled; the five others OK (Workbench accounts may WARN for a hub user without an enabled account); 71 checks.

The skeleton version and its approval are on the policy history (draft_created, submitted, approved, applied, apply_deferred with target workbench, then applied with resumed), shown in the Access Policy's History tab. The move logs to logs/deploy-workbench-<time>.log (the volume listing, the Keycloak answer, each copy and what is left), the switchover's other steps to their own logs, the test to logs/iam-research-<time>.log. Keycloak's admin events record the client's change. Nothing about the notebook's reads is recorded on the platform: the lake holds no person. Write the date, the commit, the version number, the homes copied, the snapshot and lineage step 4 printed, the hub's log lines about Secrets (there must be none refused) and the health lines under Last done; record D1 = A2 as evidenced in the decision record.

Refusals worth trying.

  • The administrator's own workspace (step 7).
  • A held-out range: bio_test asks for the range of reservation #1, md.measurements("UNIT01", "ZONE01", start="2026-11-15T10:00Z", end="2026-11-15T17:00Z"): an empty table, and md.holds() lists the range (without who or why).
  • The configuration API from a notebook: in a terminal of the workspace, curl -m 5 http://config-api.medcea.svc.cluster.local:3000/ ends with a timeout (exit 28), not an answer.
  • A pinned lineage that is not the snapshot's: md.use_snapshot(1, expect="0"*64) raises AccessError.

Afterwards. The old homes in medcea stay until the administrator removes them, once the people have checked their files (the move's last lines say how). Stop the test workspace. The skeleton version is never rolled back.

E44 The scientists' live data and Superset end

Goal. Apply research Phase 2b's change version and see its narrowing everywhere: the scientists no longer reach the Run Monitor, Superset is stopped with its card greyed out, and the engineer's dashboards survive as exported files. The exercise proves the decisions of 17 November 2026 and O12 of 19 November 2026 in the decision record.

Accounts and roles. admin drafts and applies; qa_user (qa) approves; bio_test (bio_scientist) and eng (engineer) check what they reach. The separation shown: a narrowing is still drafted by one person and approved by another.

Before you start. E43 is done (skeleton version applied, workbench moved). The engineer's Superset dashboards are exported to a file kept outside the repository's apps/superset/dashboards/ folder; note the file names.

Steps.

  1. admin: in the Access Policy, Changes tab, New draft from defaults, reason "Research Phase 2b: the scientists' live data and Superset end"; read the diff (telemetry: the two scientists lose R; analysis: every role loses its cells), submit it.

  5. eng: open the portal's Reports area.
  6. Host operator: microk8s kubectl -n medcea get deployment superset, then ./health-check.sh.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: the diff removes exactly those cells and adds none.
  • Step 3: the apply re-renders the Run Monitor's gate and stops Superset (re-rendered (stopped …)); it ends with the version applied.
  • Step 4: the Run Monitor's refusal page, "No access to Monitor", which names the roles that may open it.

  • Step 6: "not found" for the Deployment; Superset roles SKIP; the exported dashboard files are still where you put them.

The change version is on the policy history with its draft, approval and applied event (Access Policy, History tab). The apply logs to logs/apply-policy-<time>.log. E45 Calibrate the sensor model from a snapshot and compare the controllers on it

Goal. Fetch a snapshot pinned by its lineage, fit the sensor model to it, see what the fit refuses, and run the controller comparisons on the calibrated model with manifests that name the snapshot. The exercise proves the decisions "Research Phase 3: build now, fit what's there", "Plant constants are refused until there is excitation" and "The SCD30 is calibrated relative to the SHT45, with its humidity model chosen" in the decision record; the calibration is described in Calibrating the sensor model from a snapshot.

Accounts and roles. The host operator runs the commands, on behalf of a control_scientist. No platform account signs in; nothing on the platform changes.

Before you start. RESEARCH_ENABLED is true, lake-api is Running and at least one snapshot exists (E42, E43). Steps 1 to 3 run from the platform's own checkout, which has config.env, and write only to ~/e45. Steps 4 to 8 run in a worktree of the commit to test, never in the platform's checkout, whose schd/ is the live runner's code: git worktree add ../medcea-e45 HEAD, then in it source research/lib-venv.sh && ensure_research_venv. About three hours in all, nearly all of it step 7.

Steps.

  1. In the platform's checkout: apps/research/calibrate.sh snapshots, and note snapshot 1's lineage.
  2. apps/research/calibrate.sh fetch --snapshot 1 --expect-lineage <lineage> --unit UNIT01 --zone ZONE01 --out ~/e45/s1.
  3. Fetch it again into ~/e45/s1b, then cmp ~/e45/s1/dataset.jsonl ~/e45/s1b/dataset.jsonl and cmp ~/e45/s1/extract.yaml ~/e45/s1b/extract.yaml.
  4. In the worktree: python3 -m research.calib fit-sensors ~/e45/s1/dataset.jsonl --map sht45=sht45_1,scd30=scd30_1 --name unit01-zone01-s1 --out ~/e45/e45.yaml --report ~/e45/report.txt, then diff ~/e45/e45.yaml research/calib/calibrations/unit01-zone01-s1.yaml and python3 -m research.calib verify ~/e45/e45.yaml.
  5. python3 -m research.calib fit-plant ~/e45/s1/dataset.jsonl; then echo $?.
  6. research/.venv/bin/python -m research.harness.campaign research/harness/campaigns/e39_compare.yaml --out ~/e45/u, then … e39_compare_calibrated.yaml --out ~/e45/c1 and … e39_compare_calibrated.yaml --jobs 1 --out ~/e45/c2; compare the three result_digest values.
  7. research/.venv/bin/python -m research.harness.campaign research/harness/campaigns/fruiting_compare_calibrated.yaml --max-cpu-hours 14 --out ~/e45/fc, and the same for fruiting_compare.yaml into ~/e45/fu; compare the controllers pair by pair as in The comparisons on the calibrated model.
  8. Read provenance in ~/e45/c1/manifest.json and ~/e45/fc/manifest.json, and check that ~/e45/u/manifest.json has none.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: snapshot 1 with 83,353 readings, 39,960 held out, contract 1 and its lineage, "yes" under verified.
  • Step 2: "snapshot 1 (…): verified", "complete, measurement digest recomputes", 83,353 readings in 17 pages, five series of about 16,670 readings, the extract's file name, "1 hold(s), none crossed".
  • Step 3: cmp prints nothing: the files are identical.
  • Step 4: the report shows a publish interval of about 3.0 s for both sensors, the SCD30's offsets of about +2.0 °C and −7.0 %RH, humidity_model constant_offset, the CO2 noise at its upper bound of about 0.5 ppm (upper_bound: not separable from filtered process variation, and the datasheet's 25.6 ppm is more than the readings allow), about 33 delivery stalls under "unmodelled", and the humidity range 51.35 to 55.33. The diff shows only lines of the code block (a different commit); verify exits 0.
  • Step 5: every constant but volume_m3 refused with NO_ACTUATOR_DATA, NO_EXCITATION, NO_AMBIENT, "nothing written", exit 3.
  • Step 6: 30 runs and 0 invalid each time; u's result digest equals E39's (a96b20d1…); c1's and c2's equal each other.
  • Step 7: 45 runs and 0 invalid each; the per-controller differences of the table in the research chapter.
  • Step 8: per calibrated scenario, the calibration's path, sha256, snapshot 1, its lineage, the values applied and those not applied with their reasons, and the extrapolate reason; for the fruiting scenario also the recipe line (recipe 2, step 3) and the photoperiod it replaced.

Nothing is recorded on the platform: the fetch only reads lake-api, through the host's path to it, and each calibrate.sh run logs to logs/research-calibrate-<time>.log. The evidence is the folders and the manifests. Write the date, the commit, the dataset's content_sha256, the result digests and the refusal texts under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. Each exits 2 and writes nothing (step 5's exit 3 is the plant's refusal).

  • A wrong lineage: step 2 with 64 zeros as --expect-lineage: "snapshot 1 has lineage …, not the 0000… you expected: it is not the same data".
  • A snapshot that does not exist: --snapshot 99: "no snapshot 99 in the lake (snapshots lists them)".
  • One byte changed in a copy of the calibration file, used by a copy of the smoke scenario: "calibration … sha256 differs: the file is …, the pin says …".
  • A plant entry changed to source: fitted (with the pin's sha256 updated): "plant.air_flow_fan_w is fitted: plant fits are applied from a later phase (R8)".
  • An assumed plant value changed (air flow fan 3.0 → 4.0 W): "plant.air_flow_fan_w is 4.0, not the model's assumed 3.0: change an assumption in the scenario's plant.overrides, where it is visible".
  • recipe_line added to a copy of the fruiting scenario, beside its recipe_line_from: "recipe_line and recipe_line_from both given: the pin sets the line".
  • A comment appended to apps/research/db/lake_api.sql in the worktree: the campaign refuses "the contract sources or the sandbox's code differ from HEAD (apps/research/db/lake_api.sql)". Undo it with git checkout.

Afterwards. rm -r ~/e45 (keep it if the numbers are evidence for a proposal); git worktree remove ../medcea-e45.
