E46 A board whose name the router does not know

Goal. See the Configuration page's Online check fall back to a board's last reported address when the router cannot resolve its hostname, and see that the fallback is amber, never green. Proves the decision "The online check falls back to a board's last reported address" in the decision record; the column is described in Applications.

Accounts and roles. eng (engineer, reads measurements); admin (admin, reads devices but not measurements).

Before you start. ./apps/database/deploy.sh and ./apps/frontend/deploy.sh have run with this change. IAM_DB_ROLES is true (with it false, config-api answers every role alike, and step 3 shows amber too). A board is connected whose hostname the router does not resolve: on 20 November 2026 the router still named the CONTROL board unit01-c-zone01 (MAC 94:a9:90:de:74:38, 192.168.1.225) by its old name u01-c-z01. Check: microk8s kubectl -n medcea exec deploy/config-ui -c recipe-fileserver -- getent hosts unit01-c-zone01 prints nothing.

Steps.

  1. Sign in to the Configuration page as eng, open Devices and click the Online icon in the board's row.
  2. Hover over the dot.
  3. Sign in as admin (another browser profile) and do the same.
  4. Fix the name on the router (delete the old entry for the MAC, or rename it to unit01-c-zone01), power-cycle the board, wait for its health message, and check again as eng.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: an amber dot.
  • Step 2: "Its name does not resolve (the router has no entry, or an old one, for it). Answers at its last reported address 192.168.1.225 (reported …): fix its name on the router".
  • Step 3: a red dot; the tooltip says there is no last reported address to try (the board sent none, or the role does not read its messages).
  • Step 4: a green dot, "Online" with the time in milliseconds.

Nothing is recorded: the check pings and reads. The address comes from the board's own newest health or test message in medcea.measurement, read as the signed-in person through config-api. Write the date, the commit and the tooltips under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. As admin, the read of the boards' messages is refused by the database (no fallback, no sign-in prompt).

Afterwards. Nothing to undo.

Last done. 20 November 2026, commit 11784ac (database and frontend deploys of that day), by the owner, against the CONTROL board unit01-c-zone01, whose name the cluster cannot resolve (EAI_NODATA) while the router still names its address u01-c-z01: as eng the dot was amber with its last reported address 192.168.1.225 (health message of 20 November, 15:50 UTC, found through measurement_status_idx); as admin it was red with no address to try. Step 4 not done: the router's entry for MAC 94:a9:90:de:74:38 was left as it is.

E47 A domain of your own on a fresh install

Goal. See configuration ask who answers DNS for a domain of your own, see ./deploy-infra.sh check that the platform's names resolve on the host, and see a deploy whose names do not resolve end with "FINISHED WITH PROBLEMS", never "SUCCESS". Proves the decision "A custom domain without DNS records gets the platform's own name service" in the decision record; the setup is described in A domain of your own.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (a shell on the server, in the microk8s group). No platform account.

Before you start. A server to install, or an install you may redeploy, with Tailscale up. Note its Tailscale and LAN addresses (tailscale ip -4, hostname -I). Pick a domain you own or one nobody resolves (for example medcea.ai on a host where no public record points at it). No run, flash or notebook server active.

Steps.

  1. Run ./deploy-infra.sh --configure and, at the domain, choose custom domain, type the domain, answer 1 (this platform answers DNS) and 1 (the Tailscale address). Let the deploy finish.
  2. On the host: getent hosts portal.<domain>.
  3. Set LOCAL_DNS="false" in config.env by hand and run ./deploy-infra.sh again.
  4. Set LOCAL_DNS="true" again and run ./deploy-infra.sh.
  5. Run ./deploy-infra.sh --configure once more, keep the domain, and answer 1 and 2 (the LAN address); look at the PLATFORM_IP and USE_TAILSCALE lines in config.env. Put them back by answering again with 1, unless the LAN is what you want.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: config.env has LOCAL_DNS="true" and USE_TAILSCALE="true"; the deploy prints "[DNS] Do the platform's names resolve on this machine?" with two ✓ lines to the Tailscale address and "yes, to this server", and ends with "SUCCESS". If Tailscale split DNS already sent the domain to this server, configuration said so and asked neither question.
  • Step 2: the Tailscale address.
  • Step 3: ✗ lines, a red line "*.<domain> does not resolve to this server …" (or, when Tailscale split DNS sends the domain to this server, "… but nothing answers DNS on <address>:53 …: set LOCAL_DNS="true" …"), the rest of the deploy going on, and at the end "FINISHED WITH PROBLEMS" with a "Problem:" line instead of "SUCCESS". Run through ./install.sh --infra-only, the same line appears as "Still to do".
  • Step 4: "SUCCESS" again.
  • Step 5: USE_TAILSCALE="false" and a PLATFORM_IP line built on ip route get (the LAN address); the deploy's last steps speak of the LAN router, not of Tailscale.

Nothing is recorded in the platform: the check only reads. The deploy log logs/deploy-infra-*.log holds the check's lines and any "Problem:" line. Write the date, the commit, the domain and what each step printed under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. None: the check never stops a deploy, on purpose (records may be made afterwards).

Afterwards. Leave LOCAL_DNS, USE_TAILSCALE and PLATFORM_IP as the install needs them, and run ./deploy-infra.sh once more if you changed them in step 5.

Last done. Not yet.

E51 Measure the local model before anything is built on it

Numbered after E48 to E50, which the Phase 4 design reserves for its sub-phases; it is research Phase 4's step 0 and runs first (Measuring the local model).

Goal. Measure Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on this host and decide between them on both their speed and how they call tools. The exercise proves that the bench never competes with a recipe run (it refuses while one is running or scheduled and stops when one starts), that its runtime cap holds at the pessimistic end of the estimate, that an interrupted run leaves nothing running without the deploy lock, and that the day's report keeps every measurement it was given.

Accounts and roles. The host operator (the deploying account, not root) runs every command. No platform account signs in; nothing on the platform changes but the Jobs and Pods the script creates and removes in the platform namespace.

Before you start. No recipe run is running or scheduled, and the chamber is idle for the next hours. About 8 GB free for the model folder (/var/lib/<project>/research-models by default). The checkout is clean.

Steps.

  1. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh plan, then ./apps/research-model/bench.sh plan --models 8b and … plan --models 4b.
  2. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh fetch.
  3. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh bench --models 8b. While its Job runs, press Ctrl-C once, then run microk8s kubectl get job,pod -n <namespace> -l app=research-llm-bench.
  4. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh bench --models 8b again, to the end; then ./apps/research-model/bench.sh bench --models 4b.
  5. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh eval.
  6. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh report, and read research/agents/bench/<date>.json: bench.avx_check, bench.runs, bench.best, eval.<model>.scores, eval.<model>.transcript.verdict and recommendation.
  7. git status --short research/.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: the plan, R26's depth runs first and the thread and NUMA sweep last, then "Estimated runtime: … h expected, … h pessimistic (…; no F16C here: the context part counted 2.0x); the cap is 4.0 h (--max-hours), checked against the pessimistic figure." Both models together are refused: "Refused: the pessimistic runtime is over the 4.0 h cap … Measure one model at a time (--models 8b, then --models 4b: the day's report merges them) …". Each model alone is accepted.
  • Step 2: each model downloaded (or resumed) and "Fetched and verified".
  • Step 3: "No recipe run is R or S.", the Job started; after Ctrl-C "Stopped before Job research-llm-bench finished: it was deleted (bench.sh cleanup removes anything left)." and exit code 130 (medcea.sh: Failed: exit code 130); the get shows no Job, or one terminating.
  • Step 4: "Bench done." twice. The report's bench.avx_check is pass (the server's AVX = 1 | AVX2 = 0 line), the depth runs' rows say "affinity": "pinned", sweep rows under isolate say "node affinity".
  • Step 5: per model 16 conversations, each pass or FAIL with its reason, and the transcript's five turns, then "eval 8b: …/16 passed, … prefix reuse" or "… broken".
  • Step 6: bench.runs lists both bench runs of steps 3 to 4 (the stopped one marked incomplete) and bench.best both models; the recommendation names a model and its reasons, or none with what is missing.
  • Step 7: the report file is new (untracked); a campaign or a calibration would still run (the sandbox's dirty check leaves this file out).

Nothing is recorded on the platform. Each command logs to logs/research-llm-bench-<time>.log; the raw and parsed results are logs/research-llm-bench-<time>.{out,plan.json,parsed.json}, logs/research-llm-eval-<time>-<model>.json and ….server.log (mode 600); the day's evidence is research/agents/bench/<date>.json, to commit. Write the date, the commit, both models' best prompt and generation rates, the depth-12288 rates, the eval scores, the prefix-reuse verdicts and the recommendation under Last done, and the owner's choice in the decision record.

Refusals worth trying.

  • bench.sh bench --models 8b --max-hours 1: the plan, then "Refused: the pessimistic runtime is over the 1.0 h cap …", exit 2, nothing started.
  • While a recipe run is running or scheduled (only when one is anyway; never start one for this): bench and eval list it and refuse with "Refused while a recipe run is R or S …", exit 1. A run that starts while the bench runs stops it within five minutes: "stopped: run N started (status R). Job research-llm-bench was deleted; what it measured is in the report".
  • bench.sh bench --threads 13: "--threads: 1 to 12 (R25: at most 12, on one socket)", exit 2, before the log and the lock.

Afterwards. ./apps/research-model/bench.sh cleanup (removes anything labelled app=research-llm-bench; the models stay). Commit research/agents/bench/<date>.json. The model folder is kept for Phase 4b; remove it by hand only if the local model is abandoned.

E52 Rerun or decommission a failed run

Goal. Run a failed run's recipe again as a new run, and take a failed run out of use for good, with the safeguard against doing it by mistake. Proves the decision "A failed run is rerun as a new run or decommissioned for good" in the decision record.

Accounts and roles. A production_manager account (for example pm_user); an operator account for the refusal.

Before you start. ./apps/database/deploy.sh and ./apps/scheduler/deploy.sh (and ./apps/monitor/deploy.sh) have run with this change. At least one Failed run exists (stop or cancel one), and the unit has an approved parameter set.

Steps.

  1. In the Scheduler, find the Failed run under Current Runs and press ⟳ Rerun.
  2. Check that Run Now opens with the unit and recipe filled in; choose a parameter set and press Start Run, then stop the new run.
  3. On a Failed run, press ⊘ Decommission, type a wrong number, then the right one, and press ⊘ Decommission permanently.
  4. Look under Completed Runs, and in the Run Monitor.

What you should see.

  • Step 2: a new run with its own number, carrying the chosen parameter set; the failed run unchanged.
  • Step 3: the button stays disabled until the typed number is exactly the run's; then "Run #N decommissioned", and the run leaves Current Runs.
  • Step 4: the run under Completed Runs with the status Decommissioned; not in the Run Monitor.

The decommission is recorded in medcea.row_change (the run's is_active from Y to N, with the person, role and time) and in the run's updated_by_* columns; the run, its log and its cycles are kept. Write the date, the commit, the run numbers and what you saw under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. A request without the run's number, PATCH /api/runs/<N>/status with {"status": "D"}: "to decommission run N, confirm with its number". Decommissioning a Queued or Running run: "only a failed or stopped run is decommissioned". Retrying or executing a decommissioned run: "run N is decommissioned: it is kept as a record and never runs again" (the scheduler and the database both refuse). As an operator, a run no production manager prepared for one of your units: refused as for Stop.

Afterwards. Nothing to undo: a decommissioned run stays a record.

Last done. 21 November 2026, branch research/phase-4 (c0095ba), by the host operator. Fetch: both models verified by sha256 in about 3 minutes. Bench: llama.cpp b12182 loaded its AVX-only backend (AVX = 1 | AVX2 = 0). Qwen3-8B on 6 cores of one processor: 9.7 tokens/s reading and 2.0 generating with an empty context, 7.2 and 0.63 at 4,096 tokens, 4.7 and 0.25 at 12,288; 12 threads or one NUMA node changed little (best 2.18). Qwen3-4B: 18.1 and 3.8 empty, 11.0 and 0.74 at 4,096, 6.1 and 0.26 at 12,288. The 8B bench ran beside run 3 (--during-run, owner decision of the day; its rows are marked), after a first attempt that a queued run stopped, as designed; the 4B bench ran on a quiet host. The eval (steps 5 and 6) was not run: the owner moved it to 4b, where it runs against the real model server (exercise E49). The results file is research/agents/bench/2026-11-21.json. The eval of Qwen3-4B ran on 22 November 2026 (34816a7) at the production context of 4,096 tokens, beside run 5 (--during-run), after a first attempt that run 5 stopped, as designed; that attempt found that the stop left its Pod and key behind (the exit trap ran under set -e), fixed with a test. Result: 11 of 16 conversations passed; tool-call validity 0.91, spec validity 0.75, budget respected 1.0, injection resisted 1.0 (both injections), refusals respected 0.5; undeclared tools 0. The failures: wrong or missing arguments (pinning a snapshot, a summary's tag, unit and zone), a parameter grid written as lists where the spec takes numbers, no proposal where one was due, and a lake listing where the step called for an estimate. The 5-turn transcript reused most of each prompt (68 to 310 new tokens of 1,700 to 2,800). The results file is research/agents/bench/2026-11-22.json. The eval of Qwen3-8B ran on 23 November 2026 at the same context, with no run active (about 52 minutes): 13 of 16 passed; tool-call validity 1.0, spec validity 1.0, budget respected 1.0, injection resisted 1.0, refusals respected 0.5, undeclared tools 0. Its failures: a proposal whose arguments did not match, a snapshot pin where the step called for an estimate, and the results read where the step called for the status. Its transcript turns took 135 to 177 s against 4B's 100 to 105 s, and its prefix reuse is broken: each turn re-reads its own previous answer (about 100 tokens, some 15 s), while 4B's reuse held. The day's report first made no recommendation, because it counted only that day's files and the throughput was measured on the 21st; the report now takes the newest earlier day's throughput and evals and names their dates (recommendation.inputs). Recommendation by the report's rule (depth-0 throughput above the thresholds, not clearly worse on any graded outcome): 8B. The owner's choice of 21 November (4B, for its speed at depth) stands until the owner decides. The results file is research/agents/bench/2026-11-23.json.

E54 See what the policy waits for

Goal. Follow one change draft through the Policy UI and watch the "Waiting for you" panel tell each person what to do next, ending with the command the host operator runs. Proves Waiting for you.

Accounts and roles. An admin and a qa account of two different people.

Before you start. ./apps/iam/deploy.sh has run with this change; no policy version is open.

Steps.

  1. As the admin, open the Policy UI, Changes tab, and start a draft from the applied version.
  2. Read the panel at the top.
  3. Submit the draft. Read the panel again.
  4. Sign in as qa and read the panel; click its entry, approve the version.
  5. As admin or qa, read the panel again and copy the command with Copy.

What you should see.

  • Step 2: "Version N is a draft: submit it for qa's approval", opening the Changes tab when clicked.
  • Step 3: the panel is empty for the admin.
  • Step 4: "Version N waits for your approval"; for the maker's own account, "waits for another qa person's approval" with the reason.
  • Step 5: "Version N is approved: on the host, run" ./apps/iam/apply.sh N --by <your username>.

The panel only reads; the draft, submission and approval are recorded as in the Policy UI. Withdraw the draft if you do not apply it. Write the date, the commit and what you saw under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. Sign in as an auditor: no panel. Try to approve your own draft as a person who is both: refused as before.

Afterwards. Withdraw the draft, or have the host operator apply it.

Last done. Not yet.

E53 Read a control loop in Grafana

Goal. Follow one quantity of a running zone from its sensors to the command its loop sent, and check it against the recipe and the run. Proves the report described in Reading the Control Loops report.

Accounts and roles. An account that opens Grafana's reports (engineer, or production_manager as a Viewer).

Before you start. ./apps/report/deploy.sh has run with this change, and a run is running on the unit, or ran within the last 3 hours.

Steps.

  1. Portal → Reports → Standard reports → folder MedCEA → Control Loops: Sensors, Recipe Bounds and Commands; choose the unit and zone.
  2. In the Air humidity block, read the table: the rule, the sensors it may use, the bounds now, the value used and the last command.
  3. In the chart, compare the two sensor lines with the thick white line, and the white line with the dashed bounds.
  4. In the bar under the chart, find where the command changes, and check that it fits the value and the bounds at that moment.
  5. In the CO2 block, check what UP does.

What you should see.

  • Step 2: a rule in words, for example "Uses sht45_1; falls back to scd30_1 when it is stale · readings older than 20 s are ignored", and the bounds of the recipe step now running, with its step and cycle.
  • Step 3: the white line on the reference sensor's line (on the fallback's while the reference is stale); the dashed bounds stepping at each recipe step.
  • Step 4: below the band, UP; above it, DOWN (for temperature, cooling); held where a reading was missing.
  • Step 5: "UP: fresh-air fan on (lowers CO₂)".

Nothing is recorded: the report reads the readings, the commands the run sent and the cycles' recorded parameters, as Grafana's read-only database account. Write the date, the commit, the run and what you saw under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. An account whose role Grafana does not admit (an operator) is refused at Grafana's sign-in.

Afterwards. Nothing to undo.

Last done. Not yet.

E48 Supervise and replay a scripted agent campaign

Goal. Run the scripted agent profile compare_controllers from a notebook, approve its campaign at the gate, read its result, replay it, and see the trace anchored by a backup. Proves Agent sessions.

Accounts and roles. A control_scientist with a person id of its own (create it first, then have qa confirm the grant), a qa account (holds no cell on the agent group), an engineer (reads only). Also a bio_scientist to try the second refusal.

Before you start. The access policy version that adds the zones and the group research_campaigns is applied; ./deploy-infra.sh has created the two namespaces and the Keycloak client research-agent; ./apps/database/deploy.sh, ./apps/research/deploy.sh and ./apps/research-agents/deploy.sh have run; ./apps/backup/deploy.sh has run since; health shows 76 checks with the five new ones OK or SKIP. No recipe run is starting.

Steps.

  1. As the control scientist, in the AI Workbench copy medcea-examples/03-agent-campaign.ipynb to your home folder (the bio scientist uses 04-agent-other-session.ipynb), or open a notebook and run from medcea_agent import Client; c = Client(); c.signin(), and complete the device code in the browser.
  2. sid = c.start("compare_controllers"), then c.watch(sid).
  3. The campaign of compare_controllers is small (under 2 CPU-hours) and starts without asking. Keep watching.
  4. Keep watching until the session stops with the reason finished.
  5. c.replay(sid) once the session has stopped: the orchestrator runs Job replay-<id> and the call returns its verdict.
  6. On the host, ./apps/backup/backups.sh now, then ./health-check.sh.
  7. The gate: sid2 = c.start("gate_check"), then c.watch(sid2). Its campaign (six runs of a 9,000-hour fruiting scenario) estimates about 3 CPU-hours, so it waits. Note the gate id the watch prints.
  8. As the bio scientist, in their own notebook: c.answer("<sid2>", "gates", "<gid>", "approve").
  9. As the control scientist: c.answer(sid2, "gates", gid, "approve", cap_h=0.05), and keep watching until the session stops.

What you should see.

  • Step 1: your name after sign-in, never a token. Step 2: a session id; the first events are the lake listing and the estimate.
  • Step 3: the campaign starts as Job sim-<id> in the agents namespace, gate auto.
  • Step 5: replay verdict ok.
  • Step 6: Agent trace chain OK, Agent trace anchor OK naming the event the backup recorded, Agent sessions OK.
  • Step 7: gate_pending with the estimate and a cap; the agent waits (wall time, no turns spent).
  • Step 8: refused, 404 "no such session": a person sees and answers only their own sessions.
  • Step 9: a Job sim-<id> starts with the approved 0.05 CPU-hour cap and is stopped by its watchdog (cpu_cap_exceeded); the agent gets the failure as a tool result and the session stops finished. Approving without cap_h would run the whole campaign (about 3 CPU-hours); "deny" sends the agent "the supervisor denied this campaign".

Every turn, call, result, gate decision and the stop is an event in agent_trace.event of database medcea_research (the person's sub and role on each), chained by hash; the backup's MANIFEST has the line # agent_trace chain head (read before the dump): <event> <hash> db=<system id>/<oid>. Write the date, the commit, the session id and the event numbers under Last done.

Refusals worth trying. The engineer's c.start(...) is refused (403). The bio scientist approving the control scientist's gate is refused (404, step 8). A revoked session token at mcp-sim answers 401, and a claim token used twice is refused. A campaign above the session's budget never starts.

Afterwards. c.stop(sid) if the session is still active; remove old code bundles with the deploy's own option when that exists. The trace stays.

Last done. Partly, 22 November 2026, commit 874aa85 (policy versions 10 and 11), account cs_user (control_scientist): session 119–155 ran the lake listing, the estimate (3 runs, 0.0002 CPU-hours, gate auto), simulation Job sim-cdbb3360ea86f14e21e84 (result digest dc63ff8c…, all three runs valid) and the PID proposal, and stopped with reason finished; the strict replay of its 25 agent events was ok (run on the host with research/agents/replay.py: the replay Job is not built, so c.replay answers 501); backup 20261122-134859Z recorded agent_trace head 155, and health showed Agent trace chain, Agent trace anchor and Agent sessions OK. Not yet: a gate that waits for the supervisor (needs a campaign of 2 CPU-hours or more), the refusals. The run found and fixed nine defects on the way (sign-in relay address and port, the cluster CA under Python 3.14, the claim racing the pod registration, the MCP protocol version, the loader without git, the deadline of a small campaign, the replay matching server records); the CPU cap was not enforced on the small campaign (0.001 against 0.0002 CPU-hours: the run ended between two watchdog looks), and snapshot lineages showed as "?" in the lake listing; both fixed the same day (a final cap check, a 0.01 CPU-hour floor on the cap, 64-hex lineages), to be confirmed by the next run. Later the same day, commit 1689950 then c2f527d/6bfe3d1 (policy version 12): c.replay through the replay Job reproduced the scripted session (24 agent events, ok); the local model (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, profile compare_controllers_local, account cs_test) ran two sessions (events 189–208 and 209–230), each four turns of 34–92 s through the model gateway with three sim.estimate calls and a stop with reason finished but no sim.run: the 4B model priced campaigns and did not run one; the strict replay of session GT3shBlERKRW9ac59_7tEA (7 agent events, its requests checked against the gateway's) was ok. That run found that the session's token spend read 0 (the counts sit under usage), so the token budget was not enforced; fixed (6bfe3d1), the session then read 4,857 prompt and 313 output tokens.

Adding an exercise

Every change a user would notice gets an exercise in this chapter, in the same piece of work as the change: a new screen, button, rule or refusal. Extend an exercise when the change belongs to it; add a new one (E9, E10 and so on) when it does not.

  1. Write it in the form of How every exercise is written, all nine parts. Take the screen, tab, button and field names and the refusal texts from the code, not from memory.
  2. Add its row to Exercises at a glance: exercise, roles, what it proves, last done ("Not yet").
  3. After the change is deployed, run the exercise on the platform.
  4. Write the date and the result under Last done and in the summary row, with the record numbers the screens showed (approval, decision, pending change). Never write a number you did not see.
  5. When the exercise is evidence that a control works, record it in the decision record as well, and list anything it found in known gaps.

Reference

Lookup tables for everyday use: the web addresses and who may open them, the roles each application admits, the access levels and resource groups of the access policy, the settings an administrator may change, the scripts on the platform host, the health checks, and the abbreviations used in this manual. The tables describe the platform as of IAM 2.6, deployed report-only on 31 October 2026, with the access policy at its default version.

The access policy also names an Access Policy host (POLICY_DOMAIN, for admin, qa, qp and auditor). Its address is POLICY_DOMAIN (policy.$DOMAIN); it is deployed by ./apps/iam/deploy.sh since IAM 4.3, and on a fresh install from 8 November 2026 on, since IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES is then true. With IAM_GATES="false" the compiled hosts fall back to the pre-policy list operator, qa, auditor, admin. Sensor and control boards do not use a web address: they reach the MQTT broker over TLS on port 31884 of the platform host (the plain port 31883 is closed since 5 November 2026).

Opening an application is only the first gate. What you may do on the page is decided by your access levels on each resource group, checked by the service and by the database.

Access levels

Every cell of the access policy holds zero or more of these levels. A level that "includes" others gives them too.

LetterNameIncludesMeaning
NNoneNo access. The role does not see the resource at all. The default for every cell.
RReadSee the resource, change nothing.
XRead and exportRRead, and take a copy out of the platform through the Database Management export. Each export is recorded with who exported which objects and when.
CCreateRAdd new records; never change existing ones. Used for appending to regulated data and audit trails.
UUpdateC, RCreate and change records, within the group's constraint. On recipes and controllers only while the record is a draft. Removing a configuration record means setting it to "retired", never deleting it. Never given to a person on regulated or history data.
AApproveRApprove or release another person's work. The approver must be a different person from the author. In this version an approval is an attributable, time-stamped record, not a 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature.
OOperateRStart, stop or trigger a process (execute a run, stop it, trigger a schedule) without changing its definition.
KConfigureAdminister the tool without the content it holds. On accounts it means reading and changing account records, which are personal data. Held only by admin.
DDeleteRemove platform components and releases on the host. Never data. Held only by admin.

Tools with their own database account. Grafana (group dashboards, account svc_grafana) and Superset (group analysis, account svc_superset) read through an account of their own, not as the person, so what limits a person there is that account's grants. analysis's Superset tool gives Superset's Alpha with SQL Lab for U (the builders bio_scientist, control_scientist, engineer, who hold R, C and U) and Gamma with "MedCEA Viewer" for R (the viewers production_manager, qc, qp); any other role cannot sign in, and Superset's Admin role is never given. svc_superset's ceiling is master data and telemetry, read only, with no runs (decision D7): SELECT on 11 tables and views of schema medcea, EXECUTE on medcea.unit_commissioning() and a row rule on medcea.measurement that admits every row, so a Superset user sees every unit's telemetry. Its password is SVC_SUPERSET_DB_PASS, written into Secret db-svc-superset by ./apps/database/deploy.sh. Superset's own metadata database (superset, owned by superset_meta) is outside the platform database and the policy.

Access policy versions (IAM 4.1 to 4.5)

Since slice 4.1 the database holds everything Phase 4 needs to keep the access policy as numbered versions (migration 008c). Since slice 4.2a version 1 exists (the factory policy, applied by ./apps/iam/apply.sh --bootstrap inside the iam deploy), every deploy compiles from the applied version, and every deploy runs the skeleton gate (see The applied access policy). Since slice 4.3 the Access Policy shows the versions, and since slice 4.4 an admin drafts change versions there and a qa person approves them; applying an approved version is slice 4.5.

ObjectWhat it is
iam_policy.versionOne row per version: kind (bootstrap, change, skeleton, rollback), status (draft, submitted, approved, applied, superseded, withdrawn), who drafted, submitted, approved, applied, confirmed or disputed it, and its digests. At most one change or skeleton version is open at a time (one_open).
iam_policy.entryThe matrix of a version, one row per role, group and level, with the constraint that narrows that level.
iam_policy.waiverThe version's waivers, with the objects each one covers.
iam_policy.skeletonPlatform skeletons (everything of the policy but the matrix and waivers) by digest; the one this host accepted last is in force.
iam_policy.version_diffFor a skeleton version, the diff the host computed, shown to qa byte for byte.
iam_policy.approval_evidenceThe signed token behind every approve, return, confirm and dispute. Readable by the database owner only.

The six tables are written only by the policy's own database functions. A trigger refuses anything else, for every role, the database owner included: no update without the function's mark, no delete (except replacing a cell of a draft), no truncate, one step of the state machine per update, and every status change written to the policy history (status_changed).

FunctionWho may call itRefusals
iam_policy.new_draft, save_entry, submit, withdrawiam-api (iam_svc) for a signed-in admin (C or U on iam_policy)Not the Policy UI's own person, or a blank person_id: refused. Access changed since the person signed in: "your access changed since you signed in: reload the page". No applied version, or one being applied: refused. Another version open: refused.
medcea.approve_policy, return_policy, confirm_policy, dispute_policyA qa person through the configuration API (PostgREST), with their own token of the policy hostAny other sign-in: "approve access-policy versions in the Policy UI". An author of the version (by account or person): refused. A stale base, changed entries, or another platform skeleton than this host accepted: refused, reload. The person apply.sh recorded may not confirm. Since 4.4 an approval is also refused while a policy break-glass is open, and for a skeleton version without the attestation, when it was proposed against an older accepted skeleton, or when it widens the approver's role.
iam_policy.why_not, entries_digest, audit_versionsRoles that read iam_policy (and iam-api, and Database Management's account)Read only.
iam._changed_sinceiam-apiRead only: whether a person's access changed since their token was issued. Installed by ./apps/access/deploy.sh.
iam_policy.append_historyiam-api (since 4.2a only mqtt_credential_issued), and the platform's own scripts as postgresAny event a policy version is read from (draft_created, submitted, approved, applied, apply_started, status_changed, break_glass_ended, every name starting apply_, skeleton_, waiver_, break_glass_, bootstrap_ or policy_, in any letter case): "is a policy version event, written only by the policy functions". From iam-api's account any other event than mqtt_credential_issued: "append_history: iam_svc writes only mqtt_credential_issued". A version in the payload is dropped. So whoever holds iam-api's database password cannot record a version as applied, approved or authored.
iam_policy._system_as (4.2a)The policy's own functions (database owner only)Sets the system actor of the transaction when none is set, accepts one of the allowed ones, and refuses any other: "the policy is built and applied by …, not by …". apply.sh acts as system:apply; a deploy's skeleton gate and its records as system:deploy. Accepting and syncing a skeleton allow both; building, applying and reverting a version only system:apply.
iam_policy._record (4.2a rules)The scripts as postgres, through apply.sh and dba_record_eventapplied, partial_apply, bootstrap_applied and apply_deferred: only system:apply, with a version number. break_glass_seen, break_glass_ended and account_seeded: system:apply or system:deploy; a missing version is filled in with the applied version. A policy break-glass (source: file) needs a version and a reason. An account_seeded needs username, sub, fact and a fact_id equal to the hash of its content (refused otherwise); the same content is recorded once.

The configuration API accepts tokens of the policy host's client (policy) for exactly these four calls, by POST, and nothing else: no read and no other write. The network entry is network.clients.iam-approvals with only_rpc in the policy. A qa token of the Configuration UI cannot approve a policy version either.

The route table (routes.json) gains dual_control: the roles that may approve and the roles that make changes on iam_policy and on iam_users (today qa and admin for both). Since IAM 4.5 the User Manager (who may confirm an account decision, I17) and apply.sh (who may approve a version, who is a maker) read it from there; without the key the User Manager keeps today's roles (qa approves, admin makes) and logs it once.

What a policy apply compiles (IAM 4.5). The database transaction of apply.sh N compiles the grants and the policy's functions from version N itself, not from the host file of the version before: apply.sh stages N's host file in its own mode-700 directory, binds it to the database rows (the entries digest recomputed in SQL and in Python, the body recomputed from the rows) and passes it with its SHA-256 to the database deploy's bundle, which compiles it with cli.py --staged FILE. --staged reads the file with every check of a host file and refuses (exit 2) unless its SHA-256 equals the one apply.sh pinned, and the bundle honours it only under the run's own verified deploy lock: a variable exported in a shell compiles nothing. It is not --file: an unchecked YAML file is never accepted.

python3 apps/iam/compiler/cli.py audit-version --record F (run by apply.sh --audit N, read-only) reproduces an applied version from its record: the compiler of the commit its apply_started names (git archive; its digest must be the recorded one), the version's rows composed with the skeleton it was applied under, the checker, the approval token against the jwk recorded at apply, and every artefact digest against the applied event. It prints one line per check (OK, FAIL, CANNOT) and exits 0 reproduced, 1 a mismatch, 2 cannot reproduce.

Since 4.2a the route table's digest no longer counts its source (the name of the policy it was compiled from) or applied_version: both are still in routes.json, but the same policy gives the same digest whatever it was read from. The digest moved once, at the first ./deploy-infra.sh of slice 4.2a. The configuration API's admission of the policy host's client is checked whether IAM_DB_ROLES is true or false.

Policy events of slices 4.2a to 4.5

EventWritten byPayload
bootstrap_appliedapply.sh --bootstrap, after its transaction (and --resume)version 1, kind bootstrap, os_user, claimed_by_sub and claimed_by_person (the --by account), git_commit, skeleton_digest, compiler_digest, artefacts (the digest of every compiled output), changed and deferred (empty), apply_log (the log's path), chain_head_before (the id and hash of the history's last event before the apply).
account_seeded./deploy-infra.sh (directly, or queued in state/seed-facts.jsonl and recorded by the next deploy)fact (created, person_id_set or observed), username, sub, role, person_id, by, os_user, at, fact_id (the SHA-256 of the fact's content), from_queue when it waited in the queue. No e-mail address or password.

(Node-RED's editor break-glass, recorded by ./deploy-infra.sh, is the same event without source: file.)

skeleton_acceptedA deploy (narrowing) or apply.shSince 4.2a also from: the digest of the skeleton it replaced, so the health check can recompute every accept.

Open until an applied, bootstrap_applied or partial_apply under the same version.
applied (4.5)apply.sh N, --rollback-to, --resume (resumed: true), and after a revert under the version put back (reverted_from)The bootstrap's fields (above) and based_on, rollback_of (K for a rollback), approved_by {sub, person, event_id} and jwk {kid, n, e} (the realm key the approval verified against; change and skeleton versions), changed (the targets that changed), deferred (commands that had to wait), attempts, pre_failing (checks already failing before a rollback), apply_log_sha256 of a copy of the log taken just before the record, chain_head_before {id, hash}, the reason.
partial_apply (4.5)apply.sh after a failed rolloutversion, kind, outcome, failed_targets (commands and lagging pods), attempts, based_on, its own reason. mixed: the version stays applied with its rollout unfinished (a skeleton version, or a revert bundle that failed); reverting: filed under the previous version by the revert's own transaction, open until the revert finishes (with reverted_version); reverted: under the version that was put back, which is approved again. mixed and reverting FAIL the health check until apply.sh --resume.
apply_reverted (4.5)_mark_reverted, inside the revert's transactionversion (reverted), prev (put back), decisions_in_window (account decisions made since the version was applied, which the revert does not undo); the reason names the failed commands.

Each status change also writes status_changed. Approve and return store the signed token in iam_policy.approval_evidence. apply.sh's exit codes are in apply.sh: 0 done, 1 refused or reverted, 2 a precondition, 3 committed and not finished (--resume), 130 interrupted before the commit.

The Policy UI's routes (iam-api port 8083)

Behind iam-oauth2-proxy at https://policy.<domain> (Keycloak client policy). Every route is checked against the compiled route table whatever IAM_ENFORCE says; /healthz answers before the check. Writes need Content-Type: application/json (415) and the page's own Origin (403).

RouteGroup, levelRolesWhat it does
GET /, GET /api/mepolicy_page Radmin, auditor, qa, qpThe page; who you are, which tabs and actions you have, your role's closure.
GET /api/policyiam_policy Radmin, auditor, qaEvery version, the open one with its authors, the accepted skeleton, whether you may approve.
GET /api/policy/<v>, …/<v>/explainiam_policy Rthe sameA version composed with the skeleton, the checker's verdict; one cell explained.
GET /api/policy/<v>/diff?against=appliediam_policy Rthe sameThe approval diff (below) of a change or skeleton version; 409 for other kinds.
GET /api/policy/who-can, /service-identities, /break-glassiam_policy Rthe sameThe Who can…, Service identities and Break-glass tabs.
GET /api/policy/history, /chainaudit_histories Rauditor, qa, qpThe policy events (at most 500) and the version audit; whether the hash chain is intact.
POST /api/policy/draftiam_policy Cadmin{from, reason}: a new draft, with the checker's verdict recorded. 201.
PUT /api/policy/<v>/entryiam_policy Uadmin{role, group, levels: {L: constraint or null}, reason}: replaces the whole cell.
POST /api/policy/<v>/submit, …/withdrawiam_policy Uadmin{reason}.
POST /api/policy/<v>/approveiam_policy Aqa{note, entries_digest, diff_digest, skeleton_digest, attest}; checked by iam-api, then forwarded with the person's token to /rpc/approve_policy.
POST /api/policy/<v>/return, …/confirm, …/disputeiam_policy Aqa{note} (and the attestation for confirm); forwarded the same way.

The approval diff

What a qa person approves. For a change iam-api computes it from the applied version and the submitted one, both with the skeleton it ships; for a skeleton version apply.sh --propose-skeleton computes it on the host and the database stores it (iam_policy.version_diff).

{"schema": 1, "kind": "change"|"skeleton", "version": N, "against": <applied version>,
 "entries_digest": "<64 hex>",
 "skeleton": null | {"from": "<accepted digest>", "to": "<proposed digest>", "sections": [...]},
 "cells":   [{"group": g, "role": r, "before": {L: constraint|null}, "after": {...}}, ...],
 "waivers": {"added": [...], "removed": [...]},
 "roles":   {role: {"added": [tuple, ...], "removed": [tuple, ...]}, ...},
 "system":  {"added": [...], "removed": [...]}}

Only cells that differ are listed, sorted by the bytes of group and role; roles lists only roles whose reach changes; a tuple is one thing a role or service can reach (a database privilege, a route, a host, an MQTT topic, a tool setting, a level). The document carries no time, commit or compiler version. Its canonical form is JSON with sorted keys, no spaces (, and : as separators) and non-ASCII characters written as themselves, encoded as UTF-8; diff_digest is the SHA-256 of those bytes in lower-case hex. iam-api serves exactly those bytes with the headers X-Medcea-Skeleton-Digest and X-Medcea-Diff-Digest, and the browser hashes what it received before showing it.

The host policy file

state/policy-applied.yaml (mode 600 in a mode-700 state/, not in git, written only by the scripts under the deploy lock):

# medcea-applied: version=N kind=bootstrap|change|skeleton|rollback entries_digest=<64 hex> skeleton_digest=<64 hex> git_commit=<40 hex>[-dirty]|unknown written_at=<UTC>
# medcea-applied-body: body_digest=<64 hex> groups=<n> roles=<n> dropped=<n> keys=<64 hex>
# Written by infra/lib-policy-source.sh (or apps/iam/apply.sh) under the deploy lock …
<the policy: the accepted skeleton with the applied version's matrix and waivers>

entries_digest is the applied version's; skeleton_digest the accepted skeleton's, checked against the body; body_digest covers the matrix and waivers; groups and roles count the version's keys and keys is their digest; dropped counts rows the skeleton no longer has a group or role for. A rewrite happens only when the version, kind, a digest or the second line differs, or the body differs from the database; a new written_at or commit alone is not a difference. state/seed-facts.jsonl (account facts waiting for the history), state/break-glass/ (break-glass copies) and state/retired-<time>-<why>/ (files moved aside) live next to it.

Policy commands of slices 4.2a and 4.4

CommandWhat it does
./apps/iam/apply.sh --bootstrap | --resume --by <username> [--check-only], --statusSee apply.sh. Exit 0 done, 1 refused (nothing changed), 2 usage or a precondition, 3 committed but not finished (--resume).
./apps/iam/apply.sh --propose-skeleton --by <username> --reason "<text>" --from-git <rev> [--check-only]Since slice 4.4: the skeleton of commit <rev>, which must widen access and pass the checker with the applied matrix, becomes a submitted version of kind skeleton with its diff, for qa's approval. Refused under break-glass, while another change or skeleton version is open, or while an apply is unfinished. Exit 0 done (or would do, --check-only), 1 refused (nothing changed), 2 usage or a precondition (no --from-git, no applied version, an unknown --by). See apply.sh.
./apps/iam/apply.sh --withdraw-open --by <username> --reason "<text>" [--check-only]Since slice 4.4: withdraws the open change or skeleton version as system:apply, without Keycloak. Exit 0 done or nothing open, 1 refused, 2 usage.
cli.py skeleton-gate --state F [--check], --against-git REVCompares the git skeleton with the accepted one (from a state document, or from defaults.yaml at a git revision) and prints equal, narrowing or widening with what each role gains (and, for the network rules, database role names, MQTT logins and any key the gate does not know, "section <key> changed"). Exit 0, or 3 on a widening; with --state, 2 and verdict refused when a narrowing with the applied matrix fails the checker; writes nothing.
cli.py write-applied --state F [--if-different]Writes the host file from a state document, under the deploy lock (the deploys and apply.sh call it).
cli.py export-appliedPrints defaults.yaml with only its matrix: and waivers: replaced by the applied version's, for an occasional commit; writes nothing. Exit 2 without a host file.
cli.py bootstrap-targets --out DIR [--source host]Compiles every policy output from defaults.yaml, from version 1 and from a simulated host file (or the written one) and compares them byte for byte; apply.sh runs it.
apps/iam/apply_check.pyThe offline parts of apply.sh and of the health check: can-approve, accounts, by-user, seed-fact, seed-build, seed-queue, simulate-state, bundle-sql, apply-record, bootstrap-targets, health, status, owners, and since slice 4.4 propose (the skeleton proposal: gate, checker, open version, diff and its SQL), open-version, withdraw-sql and maker-warn. It reads JSON and prints text; it never holds a secret.

The recipe file (format 2)

The Configuration UI's ↓ Export writes, and ↑ Import and the Platform Recipe Library read:

{"format": 2, "recipe_name": "Pleurotus ostreatus", "recipe_description": null, "recipe_type": "FUNGI",
 "steps": [{"recipe_item_seq_id": 1, "recipe_item_seq_name": "Colonisation", "cycle_number": 14,
            "light_type": "DARK", "light_on_minutes": 0, "light_off_minutes": 1440,
            "setpoints": {"air_temperature": {"lower": 22, "upper": 25},
                          "air_humidity": {"lower": 85, "upper": 95},
                          "co2": {"lower": 400, "upper": 5000}},
            "notes": "…"}]}

An older file (format 1) has no format or recipe_type and the eight limit columns on each step (air_temperature_lower_limit … substrate_temperature_upper_limit, hr_* for humidity); its import asks for the recipe type and maps the limits to setpoints (substrate only when both are present).

Settings

The settings an administrator may change in config.env, with the default from config.env.example. Change them with ./infra/configure.sh or, for the IAM switches, with ./medcea.sh, which runs the deploys each switch needs in the right order. A changed setting takes effect at the next deploy of the parts that read it.

Identity and network

NameDefaultMeaning
PROJECT_NAMEmedceaThe MQTT topic root, the Kubernetes namespace and the Keycloak realm. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Changing it after boards are flashed means reflashing them.
NAMESPACE$PROJECT_NAMEThe Kubernetes namespace.
RESEARCH_NAMESPACE${NAMESPACE}-researchThe research sandbox's namespace, its own zone with a default-deny network policy (research sandbox Phase 2a). Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, and not NAMESPACE. Created only while RESEARCH_ENABLED is true and the applied access policy has the research zone.
K8S_CHANNEL1.29/stableMicroK8s Kubernetes version.
PLATFORM_IPthis machine's Tailscale IPv4 address, else its first LAN addressThe address every service name points to, written by configuration as one of two lines: the template's (the Tailscale address while Tailscale is up) when the platform is reached through Tailscale, or the LAN line (the address of the default route) when USE_TAILSCALE is false. A line set by hand is never rewritten. See A domain of your own.
DOMAIN${PLATFORM_IP}.nip.ioBase domain: every service is <name>.$DOMAIN. Can be IP-based (no DNS setup), a short name the platform answers DNS for, or your own DNS domain.
LOCAL_DNSfalsetrue: the platform runs a DNS server for $DOMAIN on port 53 and maps the names in this machine's /etc/hosts. Set by configuration for the name-based domain and for a domain of your own whose DNS the platform answers.
ALIAS_DOMAIN${PLATFORM_IP}.nip.ioA previous domain kept as permanent redirects to $DOMAIN, so old links still work. Inactive when equal to DOMAIN or empty.
USE_TAILSCALEemptytrue: a deploy stops if Tailscale is not up. false: LAN only, and configuration writes the LAN line of PLATFORM_IP. Empty: not decided yet.
*_DOMAINsee Web addressesThe address of each application.

First accounts

NameDefaultMeaning
ADMIN_USER, ADMIN_EMAILadmin, emptyThe platform administrator. The e-mail address receives Keycloak password resets and is the login of pgAdmin's built-in user (used only with pgAdmin's break-glass sign-in); when Keycloak cannot be read during ./deploy-infra.sh and pgAdmin has no list of its own yet, it is the one address that gets pgAdmin's IoT Postgres entry (otherwise pgAdmin keeps its current list).
QA_USER, QA_EMAILemptyThe first person with role qa, who confirms account grants and approves policy changes. Must be someone other than the administrator.
ENGINEER_USER, ENGINEER_EMAILemptyThe first person with role engineer, the only role admitted to Node-RED and MQTT Explorer; device onboarding admits it and, into existing slots only, maintenance. May be a second account of the administrator, with its own username and e-mail address.
KC_BREAKGLASS_USERkc-breakglassKeycloak's own console account (realm master), used only for recovery. Every use is recorded in Keycloak's admin events.
GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER, GRAFANA_DEVELOPER_USER, GRAFANA_VIEWER_USERadmin, developer, viewerThe demo accounts from before IAM Phase 3.1. Used only while IAM_GATES is false (the rollback), which creates them with the old Grafana roles. Otherwise nothing creates them, and accounts that already exist are left as they are.

IAM switches

Change these with ./medcea.sh (IAM switches), which checks each switch's preconditions and runs its enable or rollback steps. After a fresh install, IAM switches → Bring IAM to full enforcement turns on every switch still false, in order (see After a fresh install).

NameDefaultMeaning
IAM_GATEStrueEach signed-in host admits the roles compiled from the access policy. false falls back to the pre-policy list (operator, qa, auditor, admin), and every deploy prints a warning.
IAM_NETPOLtrueOne network policy per application pod, so only its sign-in proxy and the listed services can connect to it. false removes them.
IAM_ENFORCEfalsefalse (report-only): every service checks each request against the route table but only logs "would refuse". true: the services answer 401, 403 or 503 to what the route table refuses. The administration side of the User Manager and Database Management refuse in both modes. Takes effect about a minute after ./deploy-infra.sh, without a restart.
IAM_POSTGREST_JWTfalsetrue: the configuration API verifies each person's sign-in token, so writes are attributed to the person and an expired or forged token is refused.
IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLEStrue (a new config.env since 8 November 2026; false before, and an existing config.env keeps its value)true: each service connects to the database under its own role instead of the database superuser, and Superset is installed (its data connection is never the superuser). pgAdmin then has limited rights: it can no longer change table structure or write data (use psql in the PostgreSQL pod). The scheduler's log settings become proposals for qa, which can be approved only once IAM_POSTGREST_JWT is true. ./install.sh runs ./deploy-infra.sh a second time after the applications while it is true, so Grafana and pgAdmin move onto their roles.
IAM_DB_ROLESfalsetrue: the database itself enforces each role's rights, limits operators to their own units and refuses changes to locked records. Refused until IAM_POSTGREST_JWT and IAM_DB_SERVICE_ROLES are on. Operators need units assigned first (apps/iam/units.sh).
IAM_MQTT_PERSONfalsetrue: the MQTT Explorer connects with a short-lived personal credential made from the person's role, accepted only on the broker's WebSocket listener, false: one sign-in check for both listeners, and the Explorer has no credential (its page says it needs true); the shared mqtt-explorer account was removed on 1 November 2026. Needs iam-api (./apps/iam/deploy.sh) and IAM_DB_ROLES=true.

Changes of IAM_DB_ROLES are recorded in the access policy history; so are changes of IAM_MQTT_PERSON, by ./deploy-infra.sh, and every MQTT Explorer credential issued. When ./deploy-infra.sh applies a changed IAM_ENFORCE, it records an enforcement_enabled or enforcement_disabled event there.

From Phase 2b the AI Workbench lives in the research zone once the access policy places it there, so false then also means no managed workbench: its deploy installs nothing and leaves a running hub alone. true: ./deploy-infra.sh creates RESEARCH_NAMESPACE (network policies, a low PriorityClass, a quota and limits) once the applied access policy has the research zone, and the research database (./apps/research/deploy.sh) and the nightly snapshot export (./apps/research-export/deploy.sh) can be deployed. false: nothing research is deployed; a namespace left from earlier is reported with how to remove it. Kept by every uninstall; ./install.sh --uninstall-all does not remove it today, so delete it by hand.
RESEARCH_DB_STORAGE10GiSize of the research database's volume (data-research-postgresql-0: the snapshots and the held-out reservations; kept by an uninstall unless --purge-data, and copied by the nightly backup).
